item.title: Jeffery Simmons Makes Life Easy
item.author: Tom Ley
item.content:encoded: Nothing sticks out quite like an All-Pro defensive lineman suddenly landing on a good team. For most football fans, Jeffery Simmons has been one of the league's best defensive tackles by reputation only. A run of playoff appearances to start his career in Tennessee gave way to a handful of lost seasons, in which he continued to anchor the Titans' defensive front while the losses piled up around him. Last night, however, we got to remember what it's like to see Simmons play in a game that matters.The Chicago Bears traded for Simmons last Thursday, which didn't leave him much time to integrate with the team ahead of a Monday night showdown against the Seattle Seahawks. "My first day in, I was in the building until dang near 10:00 at night, trying to get the playbook," he told the ESPN broadcast after the game. No matter. As J.J. Watt pointed out, it doesn't take long for a defensive lineman to get up to speed. One has the same job in Chicago as he does in Tennessee: Shove the big guy in front of you out of the way and go tackle the guy with the ball. Simmons did plenty of shoving during Chicago's 34-17 win, and in the process may have proven that the Bears now have a whole new way to win football games.Simmons got his first sack as a Bear on the Seahawks' fourth play of the game, ghosting right past his blocker and dragging Sam Darnold down with one arm. He would finish the game with six tackles (two for a loss), a sack, and a pass deflection.

item.title: A Eulogy for Sir Patrick Stewart
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Fans are reeling from the death of Sir Patrick Stewart last Wednesday at age 86. Stewart was classically-trained stage actor with the Royal Shakespeare Company who made a successful leap to science fiction by portraying Captain Jean-Luc Picard in theuniverse and Charles Xavier in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Stewart could also be wickedly funny when he wanted to. In 2015, when Stewart was 75, he appeared at the Just For Laughs festival in Montreal. There he gave his own eulogy, highlighting his proudest accomplishments and most cherished memories. While the language is PG, the subject matter may be NSFW and probably not something you'd want to explain to your children. Godspeed Sir Patrick Stewart, you will be missed. (via Metafilter) PS: If you prefer a more poignant tribute, grab a hankie and watch this.

item.title: World of Warcraft: Forever Is Already Overrun with AI Slop
item.author: Joseph Cox
item.content:encoded: World of Warcraft: Forever, a re-imaginging of the legendary MMO,comes out Wednesday. The idea is to recapture the feeling of discovery and wonder players had when adventuring across its world for the first time back in 2004.But 2026 is a very different time. Subreddits dedicated to the game are already overrun with AI-generated addons that rip off longtime developers’ work, and a company that helps players track their damage output tells me it is making changes to its API because of the inundation of AI slop addons.Warcraft Logs is made by Archon.gg that lets players track and share their logs of particular in-game fights so they can analyze them for ways to get better. This works by players downloading Archon’s software which records the data of their fights and uploads them to the site. Warcraft Logs makes its API available for free to other developers. It used to be mostly hobby developers, the CEO of Archon.gg and Warcraft Logs, who goes by Sildri Silentcrest, told me. Now, it’s increasingly commercial projects, which are supposed to ask for permission in order to head off projects that would break Warcraft Logs’ terms of service or wouldn’t be able to scale. “There’s been [an] explosion of development,” Silentcrest said. “Now, we’re averaging a[t] least one commercial ask per day. And I’m sure there are more that are commercializing without our approval. One new World of Warcraft analysis company every day! It's hard to keep up.”At the root of many of these is the explosion of vibe-coded sites and addons. Addons are custom pieces of software a player loads into their game for a specific benefit. Maybe they want a guide on the most optimal questing path to take, so an addon shows them the way on their minimap; or they want to make big changes to the UI. Some developers make real money from these, either by running Patreons or receiving ad revenue from Curseforge, the main repository for addons.If you scrolled any of the subreddits in the past few weeks, you likely came across someone posting about the new addon they ‘created’. Sometimes the poster discloses they used AI, other times they add an update later after being called out. There’s even a tool for players to use Claude or Codex while they’re in so they can keep making addons in the game.And with the flood, Warcraft Logs is changing its own API. “We're changing our API to better align with the applications we want to enable. We like things that help our community to dive deeper into their data, like tools that give you a deep dive on why you died to a boss or how you can improve on your next attempt. We don’t like things that effectively scrape lots of the data from our site to show surface-level info on their own site. Unfortunately, the ‘scrape and show basic statistics’ type has become much more prevalent,” Silentcrest said. They said Warcraft Logs is also introducing a paid commercial key “so that developers with commercial ambitions can support the foundation for the projects.”Addons have been a crucial and thriving part of for essentially the game’s entire life. Developers have spent many, many hours crafting those over the years. Now, AI is ripping those off too.“People are making rip-offs of my work and copying my ideas,” plusmouse, a , told me. Plusmouse gave one example: a particular design for nameplates in the game, which are the bars that appear above an enemy’s head. “Prior to that releasing I hadn’t seen any addons adopt that style of design, and now, it feels like every AI addon ends up using that idea,” they said. Plusmouse has found in some cases the code is so similar in the AI-generated versions, that they submit copyright complaints to Curseforge. “Sometimes the code is so similar the complaint results in a takedown, other times it’s to get away with it, despite feeling like my solution. Borrowing ideas is normal in addon development, but doing it on the scale that AI permits isn’t,” they said. Plusmouse said they made some of their GitHub repositories private, which they believe has stopped LLMs from using their code.Another key part of World of Warcraft: Forever is that the game is letting players engage with it in their own, preferred way.“If I can be hopeful, the ubiquity of services under development will allow people to pick their own experience,” Silvercrest added. “If they want to take their time and explore in a relaxed manner, then they can. If they have limited time and want to get to endgame content quickly, they can do that too. On the flip side, my worry is that there will be lots of abandonware that will frustrate users with out-of-date information, buggy software, and vulnerabilities.”Silvercrest said staff at Warcraft Logs “feel pressure to do more,” and the site has used some AI itself for research and some code review. “We have a small team. People are using our API to vibecode features that are on our own to do list. Should we take those features off our list? Or should we bite the bullet and lean into AI tools ourselves?” They added, “Two years ago, say we had 200 developers using our API and two or three or four were being abusive. Today, 10,000 developers are using our API and 1,000 are being abusive. The ratio has changed, and that really feels bad. It used [to] be developers respecting other developers’ hard work. I'm not sure what’s changed. Is it that Claude doesn’t read the ToS? Or is it that the new developers don’t care as much as the old? We seriously love some of the tools that this coding accessibility has enabled, but policing API use has become a struggle.”

item.title: It's Royals Hall of Fame time
item.author: bounce+2edd00.7bdc18-5mr68b7cb43ac2h04ai5=kill-the-newsletter.com@m.ghost.io
item.content:encoded: If you’re a nerd for baseball like most of us, team-specific Halls of Fame are generally a good time. It’s an ode to players who, in some way, made a positive impact to the franchise. They may not sniff the Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown, but they mean something to a team and its fanbase.Now that we are just over 10 years removed from the improbable and massive championship seasons of 2014 and 2015, it's not a surprise that this Royals Hall of Fame ballot for this cycle is capital “S” stacked. Actually, it’s all caps STACKED. Twelve players are up for election and I can make a convincing case to varying degrees for 11 of them.The fan vote opened on Monday. I am going to present the candidates in order of my opinion of worthiness on this ballot. A stacked ballot like this requires some strategy, so guys in their final year of eligibility get a bit of a longer look and there will maybe be a surprise or two down at the bottom.The fan voting is just one cog in the Royals Hall of Fame machine. From the press release about how votes are tabulated:Fans will be joined by other voters, including all living members of the Royals Hall of Fame, the Royals Ownership Group, members of the Royals Hall of Fame Executive Board, select members of the Kansas City Chapter of the Baseball Writers Association of America and Kansas City media, and current Royals front office staff with at least 15 years of service, in selecting any Royals Hall of Fame inductees. The online fan ballot will account for 12 full votes for each of the top five vote getters. Any candidate receiving 75% of the vote will be elected and scheduled for induction during the 2027 Royals season. Eligible alumni that receive at least 10% of the vote can remain on the ballot for five regular phase election cycles.It’s not the most transparent of systems because who knows how many votes are cast. Or how many players an individual can vote for. The only thing we know is that if a player finishes in the top five of the fan ballot, they get 12 votes. That’s probably enough of a push that a player who doesn’t finish in the top five will fail to get the required 75%.I find it hilarious that Beltrán is the Hall of Fame in Cooperstown yet is on the outside looking in when it comes to the Royals Hall. Beltrán spent parts of seven of his 20 major league seasons in KC, winning the Rookie of the Year award in 1999, hitting .287/.352/.483 while accumulating 24.8 bWAR. His prime was spent in New York with the Mets and he went into the Baseball Hall of Fame with a Mets cap, but his tenure in Kansas City was exceptionally good.Yes, context matters. In the instance of Beltrán, he played on some of the worst teams in franchise history, feuded with the front office over an injury and couldn’t wait to get out of town so he could play for a winning team. When he was finally dealt away, the Royals landed catcher John Buck, third baseman Mark Teahen and pitcher Mike Wood. Not great! Also, not Beltrán’s fault.Beltrán is ninth all-time on the Royals in position player bWAR, fifth in OPS (just behind Bobby Witt Jr. at .835) and first all-time in stolen base percentage with an 87.7 percent success rate. The counting stats aren’t there because Beltrán played in only 795 games for the Royals, 23rd all-time, but he was the best player by a mile on those bad Royals teams. Perhaps he’s been overshadowed by the beloved players from the Royals World Championship run a decade after he departed, but it’s absurd that he hasn’t gotten in.If you believe in that first-ballot Hall of Famer kind of lore, Greinke is in. Besides, it would look kind of silly to go through this exercise and not have Greinke enshrined at the end of it.Greinke debuted in 2004 and finished his Royals career in 2023 after stops in Milwaukee, Anaheim, Los Angeles, Arizona and Houston. He ranks seventh in franchise history in innings pitched (1,387.1), fourth in strikeouts (1,101) and sixth in fWAR (26.8). His 2009 season was one the best in franchise history where he posted a 2.16 ERA, 242 strikeouts and a career-best 8.7 fWAR, culminating in the AL Cy Young Award.He was traded to the Brewers after the 2010 season for two players also up for induction.You should vote for Greinke just so you can hear his acceptance speech.I’m not sure how LoCain didn’t make it into the Royals Hall his first time on the ballot. He was the best player on the Royals World Championship team in 2015 and their second-best behind 2025 Royals Hall of Fame inductee Alex Gordon on the 2014 pennant winners. That fact alone gets you the rubber stamp treatment as far as I’m concerned.I feel like I’m bringing myself to the edge of insanity when it comes to Cain. When you gather all the stats from the five years from 2013 to 2017, Cain was the best player on the Royals and it’s not even close. How he wasn’t elected the first time he was eligible doesn’t compute.He could do everything. Most of all…”HE CAN FLY!”Like Beltrán, this is Butler’s final year on the Royals Hall ballot. Unlike Beltrán, Butler is not going to be elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame.If you’re one of those who needs a complete ballplayer to be in these Halls of Fame, you’re not going to be a fan of Butler. He was drafted as a third baseman. That seemed to last about a week. He moved across the diamond to first and wasn’t much better. His defensive destiny was to forget the glove all together. Hitting was Butler’s game.It feels fairly obvious to me that Butler is one of the top hitters in franchise history. He’s fourth all-time in batting average (.295), ninth in hits (1,273), ninth in total bases (1,938), eighth in doubles (276) and eighth in RBI (628). He’s just outside the franchise top 10 in OBP (.356, good for 13th), slugging (.449, 15th) and OPS (.808, 12th). His best season was in 2012 when he hit .313/.373/.510 with 29 home runs and 107 RBI, won a Silver Slugger and was selected to the All-Star team. He should’ve been a participant in the Home Run Derby, damnit. Boooooooo!5-6-7 - Kelvin Herrera/Wade Davis/Greg HollandI understand Hall of Fame voting on any level is serious business. Serious Business! Sometimes, you just have to do something that veers from the norm. I defer to my pal Mike Engel for how this should work.How perfect would that be? So perfect that it needs to happen.If I mention "HDH", you know what I'm talking about. Maybe you think that only two of the three listed above are Royals Hall-worthy. If that’s the case, I humbly request you check yourself. You’re telling me you would vote to induct Snap and Pop and ignore Crackle? Athos and Aramis are in, but Porthos is out? Do you make a sandwich with bacon and lettuce and no tomato? Get all the way outta here with that. The Royals trio redefined how bullpens were used in the postseason and, then, revolutionized the art in the regular season. Herrera could’ve closed for 29 teams but accepted his seventh inning role. Davis closed out the World Series in 2015, but his performance on either side of a rain delay in Game Six of the ALCS is the stuff of legend. And all Holland did was sacrifice his UCL for the club while dominating hitters in the ninth. If any one of those guys isn’t a stud, I’m not sure there’s a flag flying for 2014 or 2015.Be bold. Put them in as a trio. (I thought about listing them as 7/8/9, but that would be too low. Appropriate, but low.)Soria is in a bit of a difficult position when it comes to franchise history. Acquired as a Rule 5 draft selection ahead of the 2007 season, he departed as a free agent after 2012. He then rejoined the club for the 2016 season. Bad timing, no? His closer bonafides are undisputed. He's third in club history with 162 saves, trailing only Quis and Monty. So he's in this weird reliever tier where he's not in the upper echelon of Royals closers, nor is he in the triumvirate of postseason relievers. Still, I think he's deserving of a spot in the Royals Hall. It may take some time to get there.This is where things could get contentious. Hosmer was a good player in Royals history and a pivotal player in the championship run. More than anyone, he seemed to be the guy in the middle of just about every pivotal moment in the Royals championship run. From the triple in the bottom of the 12th in the 2014 Wild Card game to the mad dash home in the ninth inning of Game Five of the 2015 World Series, Hoz was The Man.He gets in, but not this year.Mooooooose. Moustakas was another key guy on those championship teams, but lacks the numbers and moments of his teammates. He does rank ninth on the all-time franchise list for home runs (139). A two-time All-Star with the Royals, he briefly held the franchise record for most home runs in a season when he clubbed 38 in 2017. Somehow, it just worked. Escobar was the catalyst of those championship teams, leading off (despite a sub .300 OBP) and doing things like the Esky Ambush to, you know, hit leadoff inside the park home runs in the first game of the World Series. His best season was probably in 2012, but he filled up his trophy case in 2015, winning the Gold Glove, starting the All-Star game and picking up the ALCS MVP Award.He's 10th all-time on the franchise hit list with 1,208 and ninth in steals with 160.Sorry. Somebody has to be last. And when you're on a list of true franchise legends with World Series rings and Baseball Hall of Fame credentials, you kind of get pushed to the bottom. He was their big free agent signing in 2016 from San Diego. He was good in the rotation for the Royals that year, but later scuffled and finished his time as a solid closer for the club.

item.title: Trump Waylaid by Amazing Series of Court Setbacks on Election Eve
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: It has been the most extraordinary 24 hours of legal setbacks for President Trump since the start of his second term.The past two years of Trump’s clashes with the federal judiciary have been building toward the ultimate test for Article III judges: Would they hold the line and protect the 2026 election against a proven lawless, coup-plotting, insurrectionist president who has relentlessly vilified and chronically defied the judicial branch?The answer yesterday and deep into the night — even from the Roberts Court, which created this Constitution-rattling mess — was a resounding yes.In a sweeping set of rulings from coast to coast and from district courts to the highest court, President Trump, his deeply compromised Justice Department, and his way-outside-of-its-lane Department of Homeland Security were blocked at nearly every turn from interfering in state-run federal elections.It was as refreshing as it was resounding.SCOTUS to Trump: Talk to the HandThe Supreme Court — in a move for which legal experts could not immediately recall a precedent — unceremoniously smacked down a request from Trump Solicitor General D. John Sauer before it even heard from the opposing side. Sauer was seeking a Supreme Court order for California to sequester and not yet count mail-in ballots from a dubious list of 20,000 alleged noncitizen voters. The Trump DOJ had already lost in the same case twice at the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals and once at the district court.By the time it went to the Supreme Court, the DOJ’s list of 20,000 voters was so thoroughly discredited that the solicitor general could not bring himself to vouch to the Supreme Court for the reliability of the list. Earlier in the day, in a separate case in D.C., a Trump DOJ lawyer under tough questioning from a federal judge admitted that it was “fair to say” the 20,000-voter list had a “high error rate.” It was a damning admission with adverse implications for the Trump administration across all of the legal challenges to its pretextual campaign against the myth of rampant noncitizen voting.It left the solicitor general exposed in front of the Supreme Court, where all he could do was meekly gesture to the 20,000-voter list in California as something he “understood” from other components of the DOJ to be accurate. Justice Kagan referred the solicitor general’s transparently insufficient application for an injunction pending appeal to the full Supreme Court, which didn’t even ask for a response from the other side before rejecting it, with no dissents. The refusal by the six-justice conservative majority to entertain the latest bad-faith nonsense from the Trump DOJ captured the tone of the day.Snatching Victory From the Jaws of DefeatEven when it looked like the Trump DOJ had scored one legitimate win in court last evening, it immediately lost again. A three-judge panel of the 9th Circuit overturned a lower court order that had kept the Trump DOJ from making further demands to sequester alleged noncitizen ballots and from threatening prosecution for counting those ballots. But within a couple of hours the full 9th Circuit agreed to rehear the case en banc and vacated panel’s decision. A Trump win evaporated before the ink had dried.A quick side point on another 9th Circuit case: Even though the Trump DOJ appealed the dismissal of its lawless effort to block the certification of the U.S. Senate race in Alaska, it has not yet sought an emergency order from the appeals court. I don’t know if that’s a concession exactly or reading the writing on the wall — or, as I suspect, a strategic decision to wait to see if the election is close enough to warrant continuing to pursue the case after poll close today. Stay tuned.Our go-to election expert, Rick Hasen, summarizes Trump’s attack on free and fair midterm elections:It is hard to convey to nonspecialists how unlawful DOJ’s attempts to intervene in the California tabulation process and Alaska election certification are. These are not close cases, where people of good faith can disagree. The Trump Administration has been trying to assert federal control over state and local election processes, despite a lack of congressional authorization, 250 years of practice, and plenty of adverse precedent.Boasberg Provides the Perfect BookendMuch of the court action yesterday was in D.C., where a flurry of election-related cases were heard on emergency bases. U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson forced the above-mentioned DOJ admission that its alleged noncitizen voter lists were not reliable in a case brought by the union for election workers. U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan barred DOJ and DHS from sending any more alleged noncitizen voter lists to state and local governments. U.S. District Judge Reggie Walton gave the Trump DOJ a Pyrrhic victory after it insisted it would not use armed federal agents as election monitors.But it was Chief Judge James Boasberg who provided the perfect bookend to the last two years of rogue Trump attacks on the federal judiciary. It was Boasberg who was blatantly defied by the Trump administration during the unprecedented Alien Enemies Act deportation over one wild weekend in March 2025. It’s Boasberg who has been single-handedly pursuing a contempt of court inquiry into that defiance despite Trump appointees on the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals slow-rolling and handcuffing him. It’s Boasberg who has come under sustained rhetorical attack from the Trump White House.So it was poetic that Boasberg randomly wound up with two of the Trump election interference cases, and it was fitting that Boasberg flashed his independence by ruling against the Trump administration in one and for it in the other. Boasberg was convinced by an expert’s report that the Trump DOJ’s list of 20,000 noncitizen voter was not reliable and blocked it from demanding that California segregate the ballots of those who appear on the list.But in the other case brought by the DSCC, DCCC, and DGS (among others), Boasberg ruled they lacked standing: “Even extraordinary merits questions cannot justify the extraordinary relief of a preliminary injunction or temporary restraining order if those seeking it lack standing.” But he also noted that the relief granted in the other case offered “modest relief” in this case too.The courts universally held firm yesterday after what can best be called an uneven performance over the first two years of Trump II. But the trend lines are clear: The Trump DOJ long ago exhausted any good will, benefit of the doubt, or presumption of regularity. In the long term, that’s a tragic loss of a public good, another way Trump is leaving the Justice Department in ruins. But in the short term, it’s a essential realization by federal judges that took long in coming.The Harshest Judicial Rebuke of Them AllDespite everything that was going on in the election realm, the most searing rebuke from any judge not just yesterday but in the entire two years of Trump II came in the Broadview 6 case in Chicago.The case arises from Trump’s mass deportation operation, where most of the DOJ’s good will and record of fair dealing has been squandered. Not satisfied with its impunity in Operation Midway Blitz, the Trump administration aggressively prosecuted protesters of its thuggery there. The Broadview 6 prosecutions quickly unraveled, but not before the Trump DOJ allegedly made false statements in court to the judge in the case.U.S. District Judge April Perry was unstinting in putting the screws to the Trump DOJ in a new order that was quite frankly jaw-dropping to read. She was particularly harsh on the recent conduct of the DOJ’s No. 3 official Stan Woodward, who parachuted into the case late last week even as he was being taken to the woodshed by another federal judge in the D.C. golf course case.Judge Perry also took note of a new wrongful termination lawsuit filed by the former head of the FBI’s Chicago office which contained an extremely damaging allegation against U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros. Throughout the case, Boutros and his office have insisted that they never had any outside communications about the Broadview 6 case with either the White House or Main Justice. In his lawsuit, Douglas DePodesta claims otherwise, alleging that Boutros did discuss the case with Main Justice higher ups, including during an Oct. 7, 2025 meeting in DePodesta’s office. Two days later, prosecutors under Boutros sought the first flawed indictment against the Broadview 6.(Even as all this was going on in Chicago, a magistrate judge in D.C. handed the Trump DOJ another stinging defeat on Monday when he dismissed its retributive prosecution of two former FBI agents in a transparently political case brought the week before the election.)The interplay between the election cases and the mass deportation cases yesterday felt a little like a fable. The repeated bad faith, extralegal conduct, poor professionalism, and lack of candor has been most prevalent in the mass deportation cases. It is where slowly but surely federal judges had the scales removed from their eyes as to what the Justice Department has become. It took a scarily long time for many judges to catch on, but they finally have — and in the nick of time, with a free and fair election hanging in the balance.Now the question is whether judges continue to hold the line in the potential post-election chaos.

item.title: In Fact It's a Gas Price
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: Few have done as good a job as Ken Burns when it comes to chronicling the American story. I really hope his preview of the story of these midterms plays out as he envisions. “I’m optimistic that the American people recognize that our democratic institutions and sense of decency can bring us together. We have come back from crises before. We were more divided than we are today during the Revolution, the Civil War, Reconstruction and Vietnam. For 250 years, our country has prevailed in fits and starts, forging achievements, however imperfect, related to race and equality in American life.” (Gift Article): Ken Burns: Why I’m Optimistic About the Midterms. To the extent I’m capable of the disposition, I share some of Ken Burns optimism. But I’m not optimistic because I think the voters who put Trump in office suddenly care much about our democracy or our institutions. My optimism around the midterms is driven less by high ideals and more by high gas prices, tariff-fueled inflation, the successful messaging to effort to connect the economic woes of the average American to the corruption of the first family, an ill-conceived, poorly executed, and unpopular war, and a couldn’t be worse if he tried campaign season that ended with the president discussing algae in front of the Reflecting Pool — or as Susan Glasser put it, “a closing speech on Monday afternoon which channelled that same Marie Antoinette vibe—if, that is, the condemned queen had been a disoriented octogenarian who fancied herself an expert on granite.” Burns closes his piece with this: “Most midterm elections are seen as referendums on the policies of the president. This one is no different. But there’s something more fundamental at stake here, beyond policy differences. This election is about the people — who are empowered to check our chief executive — and the candidates running for Congress, who either have sworn an oath to the Constitution or hope to do so. Whether they are prepared to honor their oath should matter enormously to everyone who values the idea of us — the idea of America.” Of course, I agree. But, at this point, I’ll settle for a midterm win by any means, and for whatever reason, necessary. In the meantime, I’ll keep hoping that Americans rediscover the idea of America. But, just in case, I’ll also keep hoping my industrial-sized storage drum of Pepto Bismol arrives before the returns start pouring in.+ “Studies have found a significantly higher chance of arrhythmias in the weeks just before and after elections, and an increased rate of hospitalizations for heart attacks right after voting day.” How Election Day can affect your heart. (I’d advise you to avoid the stress and just not watch any of the breathless cable news coverage of the early results. But that would be futile. The heart wants what the heart wants.) (Gift Article): A Guide to What We’ll Know on Election Night, Hour by Hour.+ The surest prediction I’ve read comes from David Frum in (Gift Article): If the Dems take Congress, Things Are Going to Get Ugly. “He will get angrier, noisier, and crazier. He doesn’t care about the future of his party. He doesn’t care about the future of the country. He will want to punish a nation that, in his view, has ungratefully rejected him. Corruptly obtained money never feels secure. Trump, his children, and his inner group of close friends and sycophants most enriched in the past two years have a lot to worry about as the minutes of Trump’s presidency tick down. The worst is yet to come.” (In retrospect, that would have been a perfect tagline for this newsletter…)+ As I mentioned yesterday, I’ve been too damaged to make predictions, even in an election that seems as clear as this one. “For years, I’ve been backed up, aching, and swollen with a prolonged case of blue ballots. No one wants to feel the release of a pent-up blue surge that sprays across an election map more than I do. While things seem promising enough to expect a climax that looks like a Diet Coked-up Steve Kornacki being fired out of a T-shirt cannon, I’m not willing to make any predictions.” Blue Ballots: What to Expect When You’re Electing.“By the time the three hikers called for help from a rocky face on Mount Shasta in Northern California, they’d made a series of bad decisions. They didn’t bring enough food, and they’d overestimated their fitness. Instead of turning back in late afternoon when they hadn’t yet reached the top, they summited at 7:30 p.m. and had to descend in the dark. Their lack of preparation and poor planning, as they admitted later, came partly from relying on Google’s artificial intelligence chatbot Gemini. By morning, they were lost on a gnarly part of the mountain.” : AI gets people into trouble in the backcountry. “I think they kind of turned their brains off.” (That’s definitely going around these days…)+ “We are, moment by moment, doing less sensing, navigating, remembering, walking, choosing, and attending.” : Deskilling the body.“Google announced Tuesday that early next year it would turn off artificial intelligence tools in its popular software for K-12 students, unless school administrators explicitly choose to make such tools available. Executives at the tech giant said they wanted to be responsive to educators and parents who have asked for more control in how children interact with A.I. But there is a catch: Schools that choose to restrict A.I. entirely will also lose access to Google search.” This is yet another example of the power and influence of big tech (and a reminder of how they use it). It’s also something that will probably be a non-issue soon, as what was once known as Google search is being replaced by AI.“Edward Freytag doesn’t remember what happened on that sunny afternoon in July five years ago. But something — a deer, perhaps? — caused him to lose control of his motorcycle on a gentle mountain curve near Murfreesboro, Tenn. When one of his riding buddies found him 30 feet away from his bike, on the shoulder of the road, his mouth was packed with grass and dirt. He had fractured 11 bones. His helmet had a finger-size dent on the front-left side, and his brain had been badly bruised. When he woke up in the hospital, he was disoriented, experiencing short-term memory loss and having trouble finding words. But doctors told his wife, Joanna, that the prognosis was good. Edward, a 66-year-old middle school music teacher, would probably make a full recovery in three to six months. As his brain healed over the next six months, however, something remarkable happened, something that would land Edward in the annals of neuroscience case history.” (Gift Article): The Brain Injury That Made Edward Freytag a Musical Genius. “President Donald Trump said Tuesday that he has made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the United States to stop sending $4 billion in aid annually to Israel. It was not immediately clear which exact funding Trump meant.” (To us, or him.) Prepare for a new deal that will include graft.+ “Where were you when the A.I. revolution came for stand-up comedy? I was looking at my phone this month when all of a sudden my social media scrolls filled with teasingly seductive female comedians in front of brick walls, drawing hundreds of thousands of followers through flirty onstage punchlines. If the jokes of these Stepford stand-ups, packed into crop tops and body suits, seemed familiar, that’s because they were stolen.” Invasion of the Sexy A.I. Joke Thieves. (If this tech comes after news puns, I’m history.)+ “The Texas Legislature gave virtual schools a tremendous boost last year when it mandated that virtual schools get the same per-pupil funding as their brick-and-mortar counterparts. That’s despite their lacking the physical plants, maintenance staff and bus fleets, and many of the extracurriculars, that make up a big chunk of the costs of a neighborhood school. Stride doesn’t need to put unspent money back into its schools as traditional public schools would. That gives the company more for things such as advertising and executive compensation — and for a healthy operating profit, about $450 million across the whole company in the most recent academic year.” (Gift Article): Texas Pays Online School Empire For Kids Who Don’t Show Up.+ “Many of their engines haven’t been fired up for years. But America’s soaring demand for electricity to power data centers is bringing them back to life. Several companies are racing to strip the engines out of old aircraft to convert them into electrical generators. And data centers, desperate for power, are snapping them up.” Old, Polluting Jet Engines Are Being Scavenged to Power Data Centers. (Claude, please tell me you didn’t come up with this idea…)+ A West Point cadet drugged his girlfriend to force an unwanted abortion. Then he went to grad school. “He wrote … that he was interested in ‘the intersection of emergency medicine, addiction and public health’ and aimed to become a physician.”+ “What Ridwell will rid you of is diverse: Orange prescription bottles become glasses frames, while bike inner tubes are made into wallets. Hard-to-recycle plastics, electronics, lightbulbs, batteries and even old pickleballs are accepted.” (Gift Article): One company promises to recycle almost everything. I gave it a try.+ (Gift Article): The Wild Rise of a Trump-Backed Drone Company. “Assembled from $5.7 million in assets, Powerus has grown within months into a $300 million enterprise, led by an unlikely cast of characters that includes a public golf-course operator in Florida; a sushi restaurateur; a Democratic donor with a New York cleaning business; and a former child-modeling talent scout who has settled claims of defrauding parents.” Oh, and of course, they have some likely investors: Eric and Don Jr.“The first time Jarell Carter entered a Pilates studio, he was expecting an easy workout. A fitness influencer and a former N.F.L. athlete, Mr. Carter is able to squat more than 500 pounds. He bench-presses more than 400. But less than 20 minutes into his first Pilates session, his “legs were shaking uncontrollably,” he said. ‘I was struggling and sweating profusely,’ he added. ‘Making noises that I just couldn’t control. I was just trying to hold it together.’ His first coherent thought? ‘Whoever created Pilates hates men.'” The Pilates Bros Have Arrived. I’ve been doing pilates 3 times a week with a teacher my wife and I refer to as The Monster. As soon as I have a coherent thought, I will share it here.

item.title: He Did
item.author: Miss Cellania

item.title: Best & Worst Of 1997
item.author: deedub77
item.content:encoded: Long time no see, but I’m finally back! Before we delve into 1998, I’ll be doing a little housekeeping, starting with a lot of 8Ball & MJG. In the meantime, I hope you enjoy the Best & Worst of 1997.: (The X-Ecutioners – ): It just sounds dumber than the other nominees. (Frankie Cutlass – ), (Laylaw – , ), (DJ Muggs – ), (Lost Boyz – ), (The Beatnuts – ).Worst Posse Record: “Painz & Stife”(Diamond D – Hatred, Passions And Infidelity): Diamond D serves up arguably the driest beat in his catalog for himself, Pete Rock, and (God bless the dead) Phife to rap over. Diamond’s verse is passable, but the beat, Pete, and Phife sound godawful. (Capone-N-Noreaga): Nore and his amateur band of cronies almost lulled me to sleep with their mundane street stanzas; and the whiny violin-led backdrop was annoying as shit. (Tha Alkaholiks – ): Tha Liks keep up their album tradition of making horrible posse records with The Lootpack, despite J-Ro doing all he can to break the pattern. (Busta Rhymes –): This uninspired Flipmode (Busta and Rampage)/Bad Boy (Puff and Mase) collab was memorable only for its mediocrity.: (The Firm): The most generic, placeholder album title ever. : and (both by Domino).: (Lil’ Raskull): No Limit Records was known for its cheesy, low-quality album cover artwork. Grapetree Records was a Southern-based Christian hip-hop label that copied NLR’s album-cover style, leaving a victim of the cheese. (Cross Movement): The members’ four floating heads inside a transparent God head floating through the clouds looks mad corny, and I find it hard to believe that God has a receding hairline. (LL Cool J): The grainy artwork is bad, but it becomes embarrassingly bad considering it was released on Def Jam during the label’s glory days. And what the hell is the picture of anyway? and (Domino): Virtually the same album gets two different but equally horrible album covers.: … (Various Artists): Some of hip-hop’s biggest names of the era perform underwhelming karaoke. (Atmosphere): If vanilla was an album. (Murs): Easily the worst mixed album of the year. (Domino): was already mediocre, but Domino doubled down and released pretty much the same album with a slightly different title. A complete waste of wax, time, and energy. : (Method Man on ): It’s only right that the king of aliases delivers the dopest alias of 1997. (Camp Lo – ), (Lil’ Raskull – ), (The Beatnuts – ).Best Posse Record: “Beasts From The East” – (Lost Boyz): One word: Canibus. – (Frankie Cutlass): This gets a mention for Redman’s magnificent verse alone. – (Capone-N-Noreaga): A spirited response to Tha Dogg Pound’s “New York, New York. – (CRU): When verbal vitality carries the beat. (The Notorious B.I.G.): The title was intended to be a play on the title of his debut, , but his untimely demise gave it new meaning. One Day It’ll All Make Sense (Common), (Tha Alkaholiks) (The X-Ecutioners) (EPMD)Silent Weapons For Quiet Wars (Killarmy).: (Camp Lo)The homage to Ernie Barnes’ iconicpainting (made famous for its use on Marvin Gaye’salbum cover and the ending credits for ) is dope, clever, and fitting for all the seventies nostalgia that Camp Lo conjures up on the album. I love the tribute to , one of the greatest Mafia movies ever.Scout’s Honor…By Way Of Blood (Rampage): Silly, but cleverly unique. One Day It’ll All Make Sense(Common), (The Notorious B.I.G.).Accept Your Own & Be Yourself (The Black Album) (No I.D.): This award could have gone to any of the candidates (see the Honorable Mentions below), but is a dope album that most of you didn’t even know existed. If the other candidates are sleepers, is comatose. Hatred, Passions And Infidelity. (Camp Lo): Camp Lo’s luxuriously abstract flows over Ski’s scrumptiously soulful production result in an unheralded classic. (Wu-Tang Clan): Pound for pound, this may be the best hip-hop double album, ever. Yeah, I said it! (Notorious B.I.G.) – Speaking of pounds…the carrier of a .44 Magnum in size 54 drawers boldly and brashly flaunts his polished flow and chiseled wordsmanship over great beats, which unfortunately became his swan song. (Wyclef): A masterful musical adventure orchestrated by the genius Haitian ringmaster.Cameo Whore: Busta Rhymes (10 cameos) – If you’ve listened to hip-hop any time in the past four decades, this should come as no surprise. I’m willing to bet his name will be called for this award again in the near future. Honorable Mentions: Puffy Daddy (8). Redman (7).Follow me on Instragram@damontimeisillmatic

item.title: It’s Election Day. I’m watching.
item.author: 1axbqgdmxmrnw6o6hne4ggv0y9amawx4zt0ueb@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: A few days ago, I wrote about the storm before the storm: how free and fair elections have become a full-scale war between a president seeking to undermine and those of us fighting to protect them. So far, we have battled back the storm as we have won case after case in court.If there is a pause, an eye in the storm, it will be today.Election Day is as close to a sacred day as a secular democracy can have. The Supreme Court has described polling places as “an island of calm in which voters can peacefully contemplate their choices.”As a lawyer, my job on Election Day is to watch that island and make sure that the tens of millions of voters who travel to the polls today can cast their ballots. Traditionally, this has meant ensuring polls open on time, voting lines do not grow too long, and addressing any problems that occur.But this year is very different.The federal government has turned into a voter suppression war machine. The Department of Justice is running a vast voter suppression effort. The Department of Homeland Security is creating faulty lists and intimidating voters. Even the U.S. Postal Service tried to join the voter suppression effort.The Republican Party and its allies are filing litigation aimed at making voting more difficult. Their Election Day plans will undoubtedly follow a similar path.While Democratic-controlled states will do their best to facilitate voting, their GOP counterparts make casting ballots more difficult and potentially threaten to refuse to certify Democrats who prevail.The magic of Election Day is that it is impossible to know in advance what will happen. We can read polls, but we cannot know who will win or lose. We can predict turnout, but cannot know who will show up.This year, we have the added uncertainty of what Donald Trump will do. Whatever it is, it will not be helpful.That’s why my eyes are keener than ever. I am watching even more closely. My law firm has worked overtime to prepare for one single day. Here is what I will be watching for.The DOJ has been vocal about its ramped-up poll monitoring effort, which includes about 1,000 DOJ officials dispatched as poll monitors. In defense of its monitoring effort, the DOJ told a federal judge that the officers would not be acting in their law enforcement capacity. The judge was skeptical, warning the DOJ lawyers that there would be “hell to pay” if it turns out they were lying to the court.We will find out today if the DOJ was telling the truth. If they were not, we will quickly hear reports of officers intimidating voters, acting aggressively toward poll workers, and blocking access to polling locations. Court action will follow. I hope that is not the case.That leads to the next thing I will be watching for: whether federal law enforcement — such as ICE agents or the FBI — interferes with voting. Legally, these agents cannot be stationed at polling locations, intimidate voters or interfere with voting.We have been worried about this for some time. The Trump administration has been banging the drum of alleged noncitizen voting; they may use this pretext to send ICE near the polls even if not directly at them.The DOJ is 1-29 in voting and election cases — including the huge defeat they suffered yesterday in the Supreme Court. As the GOP’s loss becomes clear from exit polls, we will watch to see if DOJ goes to court again.If the department tries to sue, my law firm is prepared to fight back. I have faith that we will beat them once again.Donald Trump has had a circus of election deniers in his ear telling him one thing: seize the ballots and the election machines. He considered this in 2020 but did not follow through. This time there will be no one in the White House telling him no.Should the election results go in Democrats' favor, I would not put it past Trump to launch an effort to seize ballots.I am almost certain Trump will cry fraud if the GOP loses the midterms. He will claim Democrats cheated and promote outlandish conspiracy theories.However, I am interested to see if Trump places any blame on the Republicans who failed to turn out voters or run competitive races. Trump will never take accountability for his own losses, and self-reflection is beyond him.But will he place any blame on his own party, or will he just say Democrats ran another rigged election? Only time will tell.We are now in the eye of the storm. As you read this, voters are making their way to their polling locations. Ballots are being cast.By this evening, we will have answers to almost — if not all — of these questions. I am watching closely today, and I am sure you are watching, too.I will check back in with you tomorrow.

item.title: Vibe Coded AO3 Clone Site Down After Fanfic Authors Buried It With 2,000 Takedown Notices in a Single Day
item.author: Samantha Cole
item.content:encoded: A vibe-coded site that scraped Archive of Our Own (AO3) fanfiction works, reuploaded them and charged for audiobook versions is down now after the creator said they received over 2,000 takedown requests from authors in the single day it was up., a website that sprung up following last week’s announced weeks-long outage of fanfiction repository AO3, scraped the internet for works to populate the site using “a swarm of AI Agents controlling 40 virtual machines were scraping the internet for all drives, scrapes, and sources,” the site’s creator, named Ganesh, wrote on a page apologizing for the entire project. AO3.life went down on Monday evening following widespread backlash from readers and authors on social media. Before it went down, the ao3.life homepage said, “AO3, saved before it slips away. Search every fandom, ship and trope. Read it here, keep the EPUB, or let it read to you when your eyes get tired.” AO3 went down on Thursday following a security incident, according to the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) which owns the repository. The site is expected to be down for as long as four weeks. OTW says no data has been lost. Readers and authors are , unable to access the site at all for potentially a month. AO3 hosts nearly 18.5 million works.ao3.life offered works as EPUBs for reading on e-readers, and as AI-generated audiobooks that Ganesh charged for after the first three minutes. They claimed on a page titled “Authors get paid here” that authors would get 91% of the profits, with AO3.life getting 9% to cover “narration and processing” costs. “Your earnings wait for you. You don't need an account here to earn. We hold your share indefinitely until you collect it, however long that takes,” the site said. On AO3, authors can “archive lock” their works, making them visible only to logged-in users, which keeps AI bots like this one from scraping them and also gives better control over how far a work spreads or whether it breaks the containment of the repository’s intended audience. Of course, authors couldn’t access AO3 while it was down to lock their works if they were publicly available before the outage.But some authors reported the archive lock not mattering. “I had everything archive locked on ao3 and it's still all here and I as the author have 0 control over any of my fics on there,” one AO3 author .ao3.life said at the bottom of the homepage that authors could request their works be removed from the site: ”Every work belongs to its author; if one is yours and you want it gone, email legal@ao3.life and it goes.” Proving that you’re the author of the work to ao3.life required authors “leave a note on your AO3 profile so we can confirm it's you,” the site said. But how authors could do that while AO3 was — and still is — completely down is a mystery. A lot of authors clearly used the legal complaints email. “In the time this site has been up, I’ve facilitated over 2,000 takedown requests. It was never my intention to hurt so many authors - and I’m truly sorry to you all. There’s no way to show my sorry [sic] better than taking this site down,” Ganesh wrote. “Why did I charge for AI Slop audiobooks? I doubt anyone knows how expensive it is to run a server like this, especially with the amount of usage this site got. It had 126,592 unique users within 24 hours of going up, and had terabytes of bandwidth in usage. In an attempt to keep the site up, I thought audiobooks were a good option. I sold like 11 audiobooks, if it’s any consolation.”Fanfiction has become a target of AI scraping, repackaging and reselling in recent years. In 2024, I reported on how Etsy sellers turn free fanfiction into printed and bound physical books, then list them for sale for as much as $100 a book. With AO3 down and fans scrambling to find ways to keep consuming the works they miss, some people have started sharing links to Google Drives on Reddit and Discord of works they’d downloaded from the site previously, even if they aren’t the original authors of those works. This has alarmed and angered a lot of writers; whether authors have the right to profit from their works depends on the content and their use of existing intellectual property. Fanfic is typically considered fair use — I can write a Bob and Larry fic without getting sued by Universal Pictures if it’s sufficiently transformative, for example — but selling it could draw the ire of their lawyers, and a potential lawsuit even if I happened to ultimately win it. Authors on AO3 are prohibited by the platform from monetizing their works or linking to payment platforms. “It was never and is not my intention to hurt authors, and I hope every subequent [sic] action I’ve taken is representative of that,” Ganesh said. “From an attempt at revenue sharing, to responding to takedown requests as fast as I could, to taking down the site as a whole.” They signed the note: “Yours truly, a 17 year old from India that thought they were doing something good.”

item.title: I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere) - YouTube
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Genius piece of OSINT by Colsto, who demonstrates how you can take almost imperceptible background noise of planes from a video soundtrack, figure out their Doppler curves, then cross reference them against ADS-B data to find the exact location of the video based on their speed, distance, and gaps between different flights.

item.title: JD Vance’s chivalry to his wife Usha fools no one
item.content:encoded: The most embarrassing aspect of Vice President JD Vance’s tough guy schtick is that he really does seem to think he’s selling it. His recent jabs at Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrat running for Michigan’s open Senate seat, as the latest cringeworthy example. As a recent Michigan event campaigning for El-Sayed’s Republican opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers, Vance sneered, “Whatever you want to talk about, Abdul, keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth because she’s way out of your league,” trying and utterly failing to imitate the tone of a man who is truly outraged over an insult to his wife.Vance’s act wasn’t just painful because he’s such a bad actor. It’s that it made no sense at all. With “out of your league,” Vance was trying to imply that El-Sayed said something sexually untoward about Usha Vance, or even that he hit on her. But El-Sayed did no such thing. Instead, the Michigan Democrat was responding to a racist comment that Vance made at a prior campaign event, where Vance falsely accused El-Sayed of supporting “sharia law” and fantasized about how horrified his deceased “Pawpaw” would be to see El-Sayed running. El-Sayed picked up the unsubtle racist implications, and shot back on X, “So do we think JD is taking Usha with him back in time to meet Papaw, or no…” Vance may not be as smart as he thinks, but he’s smart enough to take El-Sayed’s point: if the hypothetical “Pawpaw” is too racist to accept an Egyptian-American as a senator, then surely he wouldn’t be thrilled that his grandson is married to Usha Vance, who is Indian-American. By pretending the comment was sexual, Vance simply reaffirmed that racism is driving his rhetoric, because he’s leaning on tired tropes of non-white men as threats to women. “He’s urging JD Vance to be a bit more reluctant to play such sordid racist games given his own marriage to a brown person — with whom he’s had four children — who herself has faced much bigotry,” Greg Sargent of the New Republic wrote, explaining El-Sayed’s response.Sadly, there’s no reason to think that Vance cares, because the other reason his faux-chivalry act was so unconvincing is that he does not seem to like or respect his wife. On the contrary, he has a long public record of being nasty to her in public, often — though not always — disguising his cruelty as “jokes.” Sometimes he makes fun of how compliant her role forces her to be, such as when he bragged that “anything I say, no matter how crazy, my wife Usha has to smile, laugh and celebrate it.” Sometimes he portrays her as a shrew, whining last year about how he’d be “in trouble” if he forgot to mention their anniversary during a speech. These portrayals contradict each other — is she a doormat or a nag, JD? — but what ties them together is strong streak of misogyny. By pretending the comment was sexual, Vance simply reaffirmed that racism is driving his rhetoric, because he’s leaning on tired tropes of non-white men as threats to women.Sometimes these insults aren’t even pretending to be jokes, such as when the vice president’s communications staff put out a statement saying she is so busy washing dishes and scrubbing babies that she “forgets her ring sometimes.” On its surface, this may not seem too offensive, since there is nothing wrong with either activity. But the larger context makes the dig more obvious. Before JD Vance became vice president, Usha Vance was a high-powered attorney in Ohio, and definitely more successful in the legal field than her husband, who she met at Yale Law. Early in their time in D.C., Usha Vance let slip on Meghan McCain’s podcast that she isn’t exactly happy about giving up her job. “In a dream world, eventually, I’ll be able to live in my home and continue my career,” the sad-seeming Usha Vance told McCain, after repeatedly resisting the host’s repeated attempts to get her to tell charming and romantic stories about her marriage, mostly because she didn’t seem to have any. Since then, there’s been an unsubtle effort from the couple and their communications staff to create the appearance that Usha Vance has been brought to heel. Usha had a fourth child over the summer, a choice that has been aggressively portrayed as something the vice president pushed on his reluctant wife. So much so that bragging about how he strongarmed her into giving into him has become part of his stump speech. “It’s not funny, but the bit still kills at MAGA events. It’s not hard to see why. Vance has turned his marriage into a 21st century “Taming of the Shrew,” selling his audience the fantasy of taking a smart, accomplished career woman and reducing her to a submissive housewife. It’s a trope not just familiar to the right-wing audience through Hollywood, especially Hallmark movies, but seems to be a real desire among a lot of conservative men. As comedian Trevor Noah explained in his memoir, his mother taught him that the “traditional man” may want a “subservient woman,” but he is “attracted to independent women.” “He only wants a woman who is free because his dream is to put her in a cage,” she told her son.Usha Vance’s cage is a painful-to-watch online show called “Storytime with the Second Lady,” where she read children’s books to an audience that seems to have no actual children in it. (The comments on the videos are turned off.) Mostly it features Usha Vance smiling uncomfortably at right-wing guests who appear motivated not by a love of children’s literacy, but a desire to ingratiate themselves to White House. She has also endured a filming where Donald Trump openly leered at her and another where she seems to suppress a flinch when her own husband touches her knee. The purpose of this show seems less about children, but about sending the message that Usha’s transformation from careerist to hausfrau is complete. Race is very much a part of this, as JD Vance has openly complained that his wife won’t convert from Hindu to Catholicism, in case there was any doubt that there’s a colonialist urge to go along with the patriarchal fantasy. It’s the one place where her otherwise robust public display of compliance falters. She’s even slyly insulted him, saying she didn’t need to convert because she grew up in “a very stable household,” unlike her husband. So it’s unsurprising that race is a sore spot for JD Vance, and that he’s lashing out about El-Sayed’s pointed comments. That is turning out to be a mistake, however, as it’s just drawing more attention to the incoherence of Vance’s personal life and his increasingly nationalist political views. After all, male domination in the home is how sexism has played out for millennia, but the reason that racists have traditionally deplored interracial marriage is because it produces non-white children. As El-Sayed pointedly noted on a podcast months ago, JD Vance has “got brown kids,” and “at some point he’s going to have a really awkward conversation with his kids, like, you made your career hating people who are different.” Whatever Usha Vance is getting out of this charade remains a mystery, but she still seems to be game to sell out the dignity of herself and her children to protect her husband’s political career. She went on Fox News to say she “laughed” at El-Sayed’s remarks and insisted that, while she never met Pawpaw, he must have been a great guy to have raised such “loving” people as JD and his mom. JD Vance’s mom, who is portrayed in his memoir as neglectful and addicted to drugs, also responded, saying she wants to “punch” El-Sayed. Whatever happens, the contradictions in the Vance household aren’t going away. No matter how much JD Vance works himself into a “how dare you” phony froth when the issue arises, he isn’t going to be able to get people to forget that he married a woman that embodies everything he claims is antithetical to a functioning American society. El-Sayed touched a sore spot, and JD Vance’s defensive reaction said it all. If JD Vance runs for president, as he’s obviously planning to do, he won’t be able to escape an onslaught of other public figures making the same pointed observations.

item.title: Why Erika Kirk failed as Turning Point USA’s leader
item.content:encoded: When Charlie Kirk was alive, his wife Erika had a retrograde role that was easy to understand. She didn’t use the word, but she was a tradwife. Her position at Turning Point USA, the organization her husband co-founded in 2012 to promote conservative politics on high school, college and university campuses across the country, was essentially to dote on him as her leader. After they married in 2021, she became the evidence that Charlie Kirk was living up to his own beliefs about male leadership — and female submission — at home during the crucial period that he was rebranding himself as an evangelical leader from the secular libertarian he had been.He died a year ago this week, shot to death while speaking at Utah Valley University. While Erika Kirk is still out there preaching marriage and submission, her message doesn’t cohere like it did when her husband was alive. She obviously doesn’t live the tradwife life anymore. As many people have noticed, she seems like she’s doing just fine without a husband to lead her. At a recent TPUSA Chapter Leadership Summit, Kirk inadvertently illustrated her brand’s incoherence in her keynote. Her rhetoric about being a submissive housewife contrasted with her role as TPUSA’s CEO. After beginning her pitch for traditional gender roles by insisting that “submission is not a dirty word,” she rolled out a strange metaphor. Marriage, she said, was like a cathedral, with the husband serving as the building itself, “strong” and “hold[ing] the weight.” But “those stained glass windows are the wife.” She summed up her comparison this way: “If you remove the frame of the cathedral, those stained glass windows shatter. They’re useless.”But does Kirk think of herself as a shattered, useless person now, a year after her husband’s killing? Judging from the rest of the speech, it’s hard to imagine she does. At points, she compared herself to a soldier in “this battle against Satan.” She offered detailed advice on how to build TPUSA chapters. She outlined the work she’s been doing to run the organization and the plans she is implementing to secure its future. She described herself as someone who has turned her “grief into purpose.” It makes no sense: Erika Kirk really wants to lead TPUSA while also insisting that a woman’s place is in the home. This dissonance is why she is failing.It makes no sense: Erika Kirk really wants to lead TPUSA while also insisting that a woman’s place is in the home. This dissonance is why she is failing. She can’t offer any real leadership, and that vacuum has invited chaos. In the aftermath of his tragic death, her husband was intended to be a MAGA martyr. Instead, a year later, his legacy has become a joke. The circumstances of his killing have been turned into a so-called debate between two of the right’s most ridiculous influencers, Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson. The word “debate,” though, lends too much dignity to the proceeding, which was hosted by “The PBD Podcast” and advertised widely with WWE-style graphics, which featured the enlarged faces of the interlocutors imposed on a background of what looks like explosions. One would think they were discussing monster truck rallies or mixed martial arts, not the killing of a man that Owens claims was a dear friend and mentor. The debate itself was absurd. Owens and Wilson largely ignored the substantial evidence prosecutors collected for the trial of the accused Tyler Robinson, which is expected to begin this fall. Instead, Owens pretended there are numerous holes in the case. Wilson flailed, clearly unprepared to explain the facts laid out in the indictment. The two sniped, traded personal barbs and, unsurprisingly, focused more on building their own social media brands than getting to the truth. In subsequent weeks, both filmed more reactions and other content, milking the tragedy for every penny. But it’s not just the right that can’t take the Kirks or TPUSA seriously. Charlie Kirk had been barely put to rest before public attitude toward him shifted from bipartisan horror and outrage at his killing to, frankly, mockery. Memes, some of them gruesome and offensive, began spreading rapidly. “We Are Charlie Kirk,” an A.I. song originally meant to memorialize him, was immediately reappropriated as a joke. When he died, his fans and supporters naturally turned to Erika Kirk to secure his legacy. But that choice has revealed itself to be a disaster. Perhaps there is no one who could have succeeded at what now seems a nearly impossible task: transforming Charlie Kirk, a bully who dressed up his angry rhetoric in a costume of debate, into a noble hero in death. But his widow has been uniquely bad at convincing people, even her own political allies, that they should care. From the moment she walked onto the stage at his public memorial in Arizona to fireworks more suited for a World Series championship, Erika Kirk has alienated people, even drawing accusations of faking her sorrow. Her inability to lead not only hurt the TPUSA brand, but also made it much easier for hucksters like Owens to capitalize on her family’s tragedy. While Kirk isn’t a compelling figure, the levels of animosity she draws — from both the left and right — go well beyond simply not liking the woman. Her affect can be off-putting, but that alone can’t explain the extreme negative reactions she generates. Simply by existing, she doesn’t make sense — at least within her own ideology. Kirk is a tradwife without a husband, a CEO shilling for traditional gender roles. Even though it’s not her fault, she’s single — and she is still trying to argue that a woman’s whole existence should be defined by her marriage.Owens traffics in dangerous conspiracy and misinformation, but she does understand that the paradox at the heart of Kirk is why people of all political stripes find her aggravating. In the midst of Owens’ nonsense claims about Charlie Kirk’s killing during her pseudo-debate with Wilson, she did make a lucid point, arguing that Erika Kirk did not have “to take over Charlie’s company when they don’t have a parent [for their children] at home.”“His legacy is his children,” she continued, while calling out Wilson’s own hypocrisy for defending Erika Kirk despite long arguing that a woman belongs in the home, not the office. Owens understands that this incongruity between Kirk’s ideology and behavior unsettles people. Like the talented conspiracy theorist she is, Owens has spent much of the past year directing those frustrated feelings toward a wrong, sick conclusion: implying that Kirk was somehow complicit in her husband’s death. But Owens isn’t wrong that Kirk’s choices don’t make sense, especially since TPUSA has a lot of male leaders who could have taken over and underscored the organization’s message of strictly adhering to traditional gender roles. Maybe someone smarter or more charismatic than Erika Kirk would have been able to navigate these contradictions. Owens herself manages to do a bang-up job of distracting people from the way she doesn’t practice what she preaches. But looking back, Kirk’s transformation from grieving widow to unsuccessful CEO feels preordained. She herself said a wife without a husband is shattered and useless. If she truly believes that herself, she can’t be surprised when people want her to go away.

item.title: Donald Trump’s emotional support convention
item.content:encoded: Along with death and taxes, invitations to celebrations you’d rather avoid are included on the list of adult life’s sad inevitabilities. Everyone has sucked it up to go to the wedding of a couple they disapprove of, or a family dinner that will inevitably turn into an argument. Still, most of us aren’t expected to shell out thousands to go to a get-together we know we’ll hate. But when Donald Trump demands ritual worship from Republican politicians, he can’t help but try to squeeze them for every humiliating drop.This week, only days after Labor Day weekend, he is expecting hundreds of candidates to show up for two days at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas — and to pay $25,000 a pop, at minimum — for the privilege of being seen to prostrate themselves before him inside the American Airlines Center. In the past, most Republicans would have complied, ponying up both the money and time to placate the narcissist-in-chief, even though midterm conventions have never been a thing for the GOP and likely won’t be after Trump is gone. This year, though, a whole lot of candidates have discovered a sudden need to wash their hair. POLITICO reached out to 70 Republican leaders and found that 45 had already decided not to go; most of the rest haven’t decided. According to The Bulwark’s Joe Perticone, many Republicans on Capitol Hill are also reluctant to attend — a sign, he writes, that they are afraid of being seen with an unpopular president who is “This is bad news for Trump, because the only real reason this convention is happening is to boost his fragile ego. It’s apparently not enough to have a full-time aide, a svelte blonde by the name of Natalie Harp, to follow him around night and day for the sole purpose of offering praise. Nor is he satisfied with regularly televised Oval Office events, where he surrounds himself with administration officials singing hosannas to his greatness. The U.S. Mint breaking the law to put his face on a fake gold coin, the Supreme Court blessing his equally illegal White House ballroom project, the IndyCar race through the streets of Washington, the UFC fight on the White House lawn, the attempts to build an arch in Trump’s name — there is seemingly no end to the efforts at assuaging the president’s gnawing fears of his own inadequacy. Ultimately, it’s a lost cause, because his fears are justified. Over Labor Day weekend, Trump spent hours every day posting A.I.-generated delusions of grandeur on Truth Social: images of him with George Washington, a video depicting him as DC superhero Green Lantern, illustrations featuring him as the evil leader of a robot army and a rendering of an outsized map showing America conquering Mexico, Canada and Greenland to create a Trumpian empire. It’s hard to imagine who all this is for, except for himself. The 80-year-old president doesn’t seem to be able to cope with reality, and so he is instead burrowing himself into childish power fantasies as an escape.Perhaps they hope to buy enough peace to last for a few days, maybe even weeks, to focus on the upcoming midterm elections. Either way, it’s a very expensive and public equivalent of giving a pacifier to an infant.In light of all this, it’s obvious what the Republican National Committee, which is nicknaming the convention “Trumpapalooza,” hopes to achieve: enough ego gratification for Trump to calm him. Perhaps they hope to buy enough peace to last for a few days, maybe even weeks, to focus on the upcoming midterm elections. Either way, it’s a very expensive and public equivalent of giving a pacifier to an infant. But the gambit will likely backfire. Ratings, a metric that Trump fixates on endlessly, are almost assuredly going to be low. For one thing, the RNC foolishly scheduled the convention for Wednesday and Thursday night, meaning it will compete against the NFL season’s opening games. Television networks don’t seem interested in airing it. While Trump is booked for two nights as a headline speaker, he is not the orator he once was. Now known for giving ever-longer and more repetitive stemwinders, he will cap a series of uninspiring speaker choices. On top of this, the president’s approval ratings are at record lows, especially with Republicans. Taken together, it’s hard to imagine the event will draw much beyond a paltry audience. On the other hand, Trump has often managed to scare up surprising numbers of supporters, so it’s possible he will defy expectations again. But beyond the polls, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday another measure of his growing unpopularity: MAGA retail shops and their suppliers “are seeing sales dwindle.” Those that can’t pivot to more popular merchandising themes are shutting down. One retailer explained that “sales for Trump apparel began falling after Trump’s re-election but took a nosedive roughly six months ago,” just after the Iran war began. It’s unclear if Trump is aware that most Americans loathe him, and that even his fans are starting to slink away. The president has long been a fan of cable news, but there are growing indications that he is increasingly shielding himself from legitimate sources of information, much less accurate polls. As Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan of the New York Times told MS NOW, Trump lives inside an “information bubble” where he only “hears what he wants to hear.” Much of that information is provided by Harp, who keeps him soothed with printouts from right-wing websites that often publish false headlines. Presidential candidates typically don’t spend much time in the arena at conventions. Their time is too precious, and they seek to build excitement for their acceptance speech on the final night. Trump, of course, defied this tradition at the 2024 Republican National Convention, when he attended every night of the proceedings in Milwaukee, sitting like a king receiving homage. He seemed unwilling or unable to pass up the chance to listen to the endless, empty flattery coming from the stage, along with the cheers of thousands of rambunctious supporters. This midterm convention seems to be a feeble attempt to recreate that feeling for him.The problem, of course, is getting people to show up. There won’t be delegates to fill seats in the massive arena, and Republican leaders keep finding they have unbreakable plans already scheduled that night. In a last-minute bid to make sure there are warm human bodies to feed Trump the applause he craves, the RNC started giving away tickets last week. “FREE TICKETS,” screamed a text message sent out to people on a RNC donor list. Some expressed concerns it was a scam, but organizers confirmed the giveaway was genuine.But being Texas, a largely conservative state, organizers will likely be able to wrangle enough bodies that they won’t be forced to resort to paying people to show up. Still, the need to hustle for seat-fillers is another reminder of how pointless the pageant is in the first place, and how its sole purpose is to give Trump yet one more way to hide his own unpopularity from himself. There’s no mystery as to why the president’s staff and Republican leadership strive to maintain his delusion that people like him. Famously petulant and vengeful, Trump would not hesitate to destroy the career of any official who told him the truth. This is why Republicans who aren’t attending the convention are offering lame excuses to reporters rather than admitting they simply don’t want to be in Dallas. Keeping Trump placated will become an even more difficult task if, as expected, Democrats win control of the House and perhaps the Senate, despite the GOP’s best efforts at congressional gerrymandering and voter suppression. Sure, Natalie Harp will always be on hand with a constant stream of printouts blaming other Republicans for the loss and reassuring Trump that he is nation’s most beloved man. She and the president also have access to A.I., which they can ask to generate endless images of him as a warrior, god, rock star or other powerful character.But make-believe can only get one so far when the real world keeps intruding. Maintaining Trump’s bubble of flattery already looks like an exhausting task for his handlers. Their misery is only going to get worse.

item.title: White House doesn’t want voters to see the real Trump
item.content:encoded: Right now Trump can’t stop begging for attention, even though it’s immensely damaging to his party’s midterm prospects. He forced the Republicans to throw him a two-day fake convention so he could give lengthy prime-time speeches. He holds frequent on-camera events in the Oval Office, forgoing the work of actual governance so he can be photographed sitting behind the Resolute Desk.“Sitting” may be the operative word here, because as much as Trump wants to be on camera, it’s increasingly obvious that the White House only wants that to be under controlled conditions, ideally with the president parked behind a desk. If he must stand up, he’s placed behind a generously sized podium, robust enough to handle the full body-weight of his lean. This urgent desire to control Trump’s image became especially apparent during his recent trip to Ireland, when the White House went after journalist Aaron Rupar, who is known for posting a steady stream of candid photos and videos of Trump on social media, often showing the president in a less than flattering light. As much as Trump wants to be on camera, it’s increasingly obvious that the White House only wants that to happen under controlled conditions, ideally with the president parked behind a desk.“Rather than ignore this innocuous post from Rupar, the White House’s rapid response X account called him a “sick, deluded freak.” This inspired a torrent of abuse from Trump supporters, most of whom echoed the White House’s ugly claims that there’s something “creepy” about Rupar. Part of the defensiveness, no doubt, is about Rupar’s undoubted ability to make images of the enormous carry-on bag that Harp hauls around go viral. Last week, he posted a picture of Harp straining under an oversized pack, while observing that its size did nothing to quell “diaper bag allegations.”“[D]amn, Natalie’s bag just keep getting bigger and bigger,” he wrote on Saturday, over another photo of Harp carrying a gigantic duffel bag while boarding Trump’s plane. He’s having fun, but it’s also true that the massive tote is a legitimate mystery. It seems unlikely that the coiffed and polished Harp would freely choose to forgo a real suitcase in order to carry an oversized sack like a disorganized college kid. Furthermore, she has frequently been photographed following Trump around with this enormous bag, even when the president is simply playing golf. The online anger directed at Rupar escalated further on Sunday, after he posted a video of another White House aide, whom he called a “blonde Trump flunkie,” trying to prevent journalists from filming or photographing Trump on the tarmac before his departure from Ireland.
