item.title: The New York Times finally figures it out: Dear Leader is bugfuck nuts
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Holly shit, Look who just woke up from their decade-long slumber, to work out on their very own what the rest of us sussed out years ago.Are you ready for this? You’d better sit down, because this is a real shocker. It turns out — according to none other than The New York Times — that Preznit Fuckwit might be a little bit cuckoo for cocoa-puffs.Remember when the Times didn’t used to tell us shit we already knew, long after we already knew it?Is there anything else you’d like to tell us, Captains Obvious? Water is wet, maybe?Now, I see your hands up, and I know what you’re dying to ask: ‘Hey, Uncle Jeff — why has the Times waited until all the way to the very end of the election cycle to drop this news on us? Couldn’t we have used it months — or years — ago?’He is cruder than he used to be, using nearly 15 swear words per 10,000 words compared with 14 two years ago and six a decade ago, a change consistent with age-related disinhibition.The review, relying on an A.I.-assisted metric, found that he makes rambling or confusing digressions in his rallies and speeches two and a half times as often in his second term as in the 2016 campaign, although roughly the same as in 2024.Got that? The Times couldn’t blow the whistle on Dear Leader until they had rock-solid proof, gathered over a period of time — and they couldn’t do it without a janky, six-fingered plagiarism robot to do them a solid, and help do all those fancy-ass calculations.Yeah, I know — these are the same shit-kazoos who declared Joe Biden mentally incompetent after one time that he forgot someone’s name. Joe gets unceremoniously tossed on the shit-pile of sayonara, while Donny is obviously a Very Special Boy Who Deserves Every Reasonable Doubt Before Judgement Is Cast.™“He gave up all of— yeah, it was free. WE DON’T CARE if it was free. We don’t care. It’s free. They say, WE WANT TO KNOWWW why did he give a ball room? No, no, you don’t understand me. It’s a gift. To the [slurred] Unided Stades offa Meriga. WE DON’T CARE. We don’t care. [unintelligible]What in the hell was that?Preznit Fuckwit was supposed to be making his final argument for why voters should select Republicans. The final argument he actually made instead was why he should be carted off by the men with the butterfly nets.Donny gets a dance hall, and We the People get fuck-all — while gas in America reaches an all-time second-term high, one day before the midterms.By the way, who is paying $3.46 for a gallon of regular? Here in the Hudson Valley it’s more like $4.19.Fox News bobblehead: “What’s your final message to voters to get them out?”“Poverty numbers are the single best. Meaning, they’re the best. Poverty’s a bad thing, but poverty is poverty.”Oh, thank you for that explanation of — the best poverty ever. Big strong poverty, with tears in its eyes, going, ‘sir! Thank you, sir! How do you did it? How do you make us the best poverty ever? Sir!’Don’t you love Donny hand-waving poverty away, the poverty he created? ‘Poverty is poverty, whatcha gonna do?’ Thanks for explaining that.What kind of tone-deaf dumbfuckery is that, tumbling out of the rancid anus-mouth of some flim-flam man who’s grown rich off of grifting the rubes who worship him?Yes, I know what Dear Leader is to say, about poverty, but he’s not saying it — because he’s fucked in the head — and presidents aren’t supposed to be fucked in the head.But fucked in the head he is, and it shouldn’t have taken the New York Times ten years to figure out that he’s fucked in the head.And still, the Times sugar-coats it.Mr. Trump, who last year became the oldest person ever inaugurated as president and turned 80 in June, has demonstrated physical stamina as he barnstorms the country in advance of midterm elections.And that, by the way, was Joe Biden’s real crime. He looked and sounded old — while Donny has gotten an endless serious of free passes, because he can still shit out nonsense while speaking in a mostly-loud voice.I’ll bet the Times wants a cookie, as a reward for finally committing an Sorry, no. You don’t get a cookie. You spent ten years sanewashing the incoherent ravings of a maniac.Our press is supposed to warn us while shit is actually happening, and not wander in at the very end and go ‘hey, that was kind of fucked up, wasn’t it?’Everything totally fucking sucks right now, but at least we can point and laugh at Comer Fudd’s newly-dyed hair.Seriously, what the fuck? When last we saw James Comer, the rake-steppingest fuckwit in Congress, he was a dignified natural gray.Of course, Comer Fudd’s hair was the only thingabout him, as he ginned up hearing after hearing in which he clownfucked himself into one embarrassing situation after another, all the while trying to prove that he was finally going to catch that wascally wabbit, Bugs Biden. Comer Fudd never was able to pin one crime on Bugs Biden, but at least he didn’t look like some mid-life-crisis used-care-salesman while attempting to do so.Oh well, let’s be philosophical about it. Who really cares what the hair color is, when it’s the face that’s getting smacked by an endless series of rakes?Ah, there’s the Comer Fudd we all know and love.And now let’s do us some Daily Claudia.Here’s Ms Spouse getting in a little gardening on May 16, 2016.Have a great Monday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Sloane Murphy Is The Bard Of Chicago’s Drunk Trans Women
item.author: Lauren Theisen
item.content:encoded: There are two recurring trans women named Carolina in Sloane Murphy's short story collection, . One's nicknamed North, and the other's nicknamed South, but nobody can seem to keep track of which is which. "Most of the time she just responds when people call her South," one of the stories says about North, who's the elder of the two. "At least no one was calling her Old Carolina."This is just one of the details in Murphy's debut that reminded me of the best Hold Steady albums, where casts of lushly described, hard-partying outsiders self-destruct during nights that feel as exciting as they are dangerous. The big difference is that the women in Murphy's stories are trans, which means their stakes are even higher.Edited by Emily Zhou, who wrote 2023's essential short story collection , Murphy's does for Trans Chicago what Zhou did for Ann Arbor and Brooklyn. This book announces a talented young writer who crafts stories with a vivid sense of time and place, filled with recognizable conversations and sly humor, punctuated by a willingness to stare at the abyss. But while being trans in 2023 was no great shakes, Murphy's collection arrives at a time when the alarm bells ring even louder—when we can't even watch sports on TV without seeing political ads from one state or another trying to demonize us, trying to tell people we don't deserve to live as we are.

item.title: Reaping and sowing, CEO edition
item.author: Samantha Cole
item.content:encoded: It’s rare to see an executive go from fucking around to finding out so quickly. That’s what happened last week when Proton CEO Andy Yen announced he was canceling a planned re-interview process for almost all current employees that would have checked if they’re using AI enough. This follows extreme backlash from Proton users and workers against the company's aggressive pivot to AI. It’s been a wild ride internally, several employees past and present have shared with 404 Media.On Friday, Andy Yen, the CEO of Proton, cancelled a series of nearly company-wide ‘re-interviews’ that would have forced employees to explain how they are using AI, with the clear intention that they may be fired if not using it enough in the eyes of Proton leadership, according to six current Proton employees and audio of an around two hour all-hands meeting obtained by 404 Media.The move came after 404 Media published an investigation on Thursday, which showed how Yen was aggressively pushing AI across Proton, in some cases despite security concerns from employees. In one exchange, an employee in the company’s security Slack channel urged Proton to at least take a few days to pentest newly written code before pushing it live. “That’s bullshit and loser thinking. Of course it’s possible to be fast and secure,” Yen wrote in the channel at the end of August. “Stop thinking always of how to be slower, and focus more on how to be faster.” Yen added, “stop lovingly handcrafting all our code and use AI more.”The re-interview cancellations likely don’t address the concerns of many Proton users, who are more focused on Proton’s deprioritization of security; many Proton users have blasted the company’s leadership on social media over the last 24 hours and explicitly called for Yen to resign.Kinktober has come and gone. But Archive of Our Own (AO3), a massive repository for fanfiction and creative writing, is still down, and might be down for as long as a month after going down for "maintenance" following a security incident last week. The Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the non-profit organization that runs AO3, posted on its status page that the site restoration will take around two weeks, but could take up to a month.People are coping how they can.And they’re turning to anything but Wattpad to fill the void. One writer I spoke to who posts her writing and reads others’ writing on AO3 told me that she was in the middle of racing to finish a work that was deliberately timed to Kinktober and Halloween when the outage happened. She was hitting “next chapter” while reading a fic on Wednesday night when she got the message that the site was down for maintenance, “which I initially took as a sign from the universe to go to bed,” she said.Is Apple in its slop era?Contributing writer Matthew Gault writes in the wake of the iPhone Duo’s Crackgate: “My ears perked up when I heard Apple’s new foldable phones were cracking. I licked my lips when the company announced it’s releasing a touch-screen laptop. This was a company that once charged $19 for a polishing cloth, asked $200 for a VESA mount, and sold $700 wheels for the Mac Pro. Now it’s borrowing tired ideas from its competitors and launching hardware its previous leaders rejected. Remember Fermi America, the company running a data center project in Texas? Former Governor Rick Perry, who co-founded the company, just lost his board reelection seat. Oops! The Texas Tribune got a transcript of the vote from an annual meeting Friday. Catch up on the Fermi drama and the ways people in the region are pushing back .Over the weekend, indie games platform itch.io posted a screenshot showing a massive surge in new game pages. Gosh, I wonder how that happened? : The post wasn't made without a wider point; as the account has said in some subsequent replies, the surge has been almost entirely down to AI-created garbage racing onto the platform as the popularity of vibe-coded theft, copycats and machine-built slop explodes. A that conducted 5,943 experiments across 12 commercial “smart” TV devices found that most smart TVs utilize automatic content recognition, but companies like Vizio “simply ignored the consumer requests entirely more often than not,” Karl Bodes writes in his breakdown of the study . Bots murdered San Francisco Remembered,a massive Facebook group devoted to sharing old photos and memories of a SF of yore. The group was hammered with porn bots, divisive political commentary from accounts based in Southeast Asia, and no option to geofilter posts. The administrator for the group shut it down. SF Gate reports: “The straw that broke the camel’s back was that Facebook made it impossible to delete posts from visitors via the desktop version of the website. He said support is nonexistent. ‘There’s no venue to fix this stuff,’ he said.”

item.title: Trump’s DOJ is 1-29. I’m not done.
item.author: 1axbo6tfnaika1wmwd3dme2gxugd3uvo9bb433@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: The last several days have shown once again how deeply Donald Trump hates me. In the span of 24 hours, he suggested three times that I am a criminal who should be investigated and prosecuted.His rage clearly stems from the humiliation I continue to inflict on him and his lawyers in court.Trump knows well that, in the aftermath of the 2020 election, I helped defeat him and his allies in more than 60 cases challenging the outcome.In the conventional telling of that period, I led a team of highly skilled lawyers, while Trump had a ragtag team of misfits. While that is certainly true, it obscures a fundamental weakness in the way Trump and Republicans frame their election litigation: they almost always ask courts to take votes away, not to protect them.I am not claiming that the current crop of DOJ lawyers are all-stars. Many are no better than Jenna Ellis and Sidney Powell, the Trump allies who pushed his false 2020 fraud claims and later pleaded guilty in the Georgia election case. But some are experienced litigators who have competently handled government litigation for years.Yet they continue to show up before judges and lose at an astonishingly high rate.Since Trump took office, his DOJ has filed 35 election-related lawsuits. It has lost 29 and won one; five are still awaiting a ruling.In some respects, the DOJ’s 29 losses are more astounding than the 60-plus suffered by Trump’s 2020 team. After all, in 2020, Trump’s lawyers were litigating from behind and under enormous time pressure.The DOJ, by contrast, is not trying to overcome a nearly impossible deficit. It has had nearly two years to develop a coherent litigation strategy and to bring and sequence its cases to maximize success.Yet it has almost nothing to show for it.Its embarrassing record isn’t limited to the cases it files. Nearly every major effort Trump has advanced to undermine elections has been blocked by the courts.His first anti-voting executive order, which sought to require documentary proof of citizenship to register, was halted in 2025 and permanently blocked this June. His second, issued in March, directed federal agencies to compile “state citizenship lists” and ordered the U.S. Postal Service to deliver mail ballots only to voters on said lists. It was blocked as well.In October, another judge ruled that the DOJ’s scheme to collect state voter rolls and run them through the SAVE database was unlawful. Most recently, courts have barred the administration from threatening California election workers with prosecution and from sending armed federal agents door to door to question voters about noncitizen voting.Indeed, it is difficult to find any area of voting and elections where the Trump administration has consistently prevailed.Of the cases the DOJ filed, its only victory came in North Carolina, and it comes with an asterisk. The department sued the state over a voter registration form that did not require applicants to provide a driver’s license number or the last four digits of their Social Security number. According to the DOJ, this violated federal law. Rather than fight, the Republican-controlled State Board of Elections chose to settle.Trump is not interested in protecting voters. He wants the DOJ to file suits that make voting more difficult and subvert election results. That’s why he keeps losing. Most successful voting litigation does the opposite.Throughout Trump’s second term, the DOJ has adopted his ethos. In nearly every case, it focuses on the rare unlawful voter while showing no regard for the rights of those whose lawful votes might be cast aside.In Alaska, for example, the DOJ sued to delay certification of the U.S. Senate race and to force the state to segregate ballots, claiming voters might confuse Sen. Dan Sullivan with a candidate who shares his name.That remedy would necessarily compromise ballot secrecy, leaving voters vulnerable to questioning from federal agents about why they supported the candidates they chose.In California, the DOJ sued to force election officials to set aside roughly 20,000 ballots cast by voters on a Homeland Security list of alleged noncitizens. The DOJ was callously indifferent to evidence that the list swept in U.S. citizens, including people born in the United States. Indeed, even the department’s acting deputy attorney general publicly conceded that the list could contain errors.It is no wonder the DOJ lost both Alaska and California. But Trump wants these cases filed, and the DOJ under Attorney General Todd Blanche is simply there to file them.For my part, I look forward to the day when the DOJ returns to its core mission of protecting voting rights. Until then, I will continue to fight against these attacks on voters in court. If history is any guide, that will earn me Trump’s enmity. That's a price I am willing to pay.

item.title: One More Michigan Senate Update
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: I think we’ve seen all that can happen in the bizarre continuation of the Michigan Democratic Senate primary, which of course actually ended a few months ago. But given what’s happened over the last 72 hours, I guess, who am I kidding? Stevens did a new round of interviews last night, including one on CNN with Anderson Cooper. It was a further train wreck in the weeklong run of pile-ups. It was a classic case of why, in a high-stress news environment, you shouldn’t go on TV if you don’t know what you want to say. Stevens appeared to be figuring out or trying to come up with an explanation for her actions in real time on live TV. At one point she seemed to suggest she might end up voting for Abdul El-Sayed after all, though it was so disjointed that it’s hard to know just what she was trying to say. It’s for this reason that both her erstwhile friends and her current friends have been begging her to just stop talking.

item.title: Now Begins The Wait For News About Jack Campbell
item.author: Tom Ley
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Lions became the first team this season to beat the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, but nobody on either team really wanted to talk about Detroit's 19-15 win after it was over. All anyone could think about was Lions linebacker Jack Campbell.Campbell left the field strapped to a board after making a tackle early in the fourth quarter. Campbell collided with Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson in what looked like a routine play, but his body went limp as soon as he hit the ground. He remained that way for an agonizingly long period of time while players and coaches from both teams knelt on the field. Campbell was eventually placed on a board and carted off the field, and made no obvious movements.

item.title: 10 Very Strange Medical Cases
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Weird History has compiled a list of very strange medical cases from the Middle Ages to modern times. It starts with the familiar case of Phineas Gage, but I bet you haven't heard of most of these conditions. Some of the patients died, while others were able to be treated, but most left the patient with lifelong disabilities of one kind or another. At least one, the man with the sticky skin, doesn't appear to be bad at all, just strange. Be warned that a few of these stories will require a strong stomach on the part of the viewer.

item.title: One Day Out
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: First, let me remind you: be sure to join us tomorrow night starting at 8:00 p.m. ET for our TPM’s YouTube livestream coverage of the election night results. It’ll be me, TPM Publisher Joe Ragazzo and different members of the TPM team will cycle through over the course of the evening, discussing different races, sharing color commentary, answering your questions in real time, etc.As you’ve likely seen, a final round of NYT/Siena polls came out last night and they point to the bottom falling out for the GOP in key Senate races across the country. As Kate Riga and I have discussed in numerous TPM Show episodes, the NYT/Siena poll is a high quality poll which for a variety of not terribly good reasons (largely the Times’ megaphone, but also getting closer than others in a few key cycles) has influence and impact far greater than any other poll. I saw an apt comment from Nate Silver this morning, essentially, the polls no longer say this is close. The polls, collectively, say Democrats will win the senate. They could be wrong. But what they’re saying is no longer ambiguous or too close to call.

item.title: The U.S. Census Bureau and “Super Intelligence”
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Every two weeks the U.S. Census Bureau runs a survey called the Business Trends and Outlook Survey (aka BTOS). Each time it goes to 200,000 businesses out of 1.2 million total - the surveyed group (a "panel") cycles such that an individual business only completes the survey every twelve weeks.The latest data is published on alternating Thursdays at 10am.I used the most recent numbers (published October 22, 2026) to create a new version (GPT-6 Astra Extra High transcript) of the AI adoption chart, updated to reflect both the last twelve months and a change that was made to the survey question sent out by the Bureau:For comparison, here's that AI adoption chart from last year (my GPT-5 version): In September 2025 the largest (250+ employees) companies answered "yes" around 12% of the time to the question about whether they used AI in "producing goods or services".Under the new "any business function" wording, by February 2026, those same large companies answered "yes" around 30% of the time, and by October 2026 that had increased to around 40%.The data in the above chart comes from the "Employment size class" XLSX file, available from here. Here's a copy of the file I used.The changing language of the questionsAs the chart demonstrates, the question asked by the Bureau changed in a material way on November 17th, 2025. Prior to that date, the question they asked was this (emphasis mine):In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in producing goods or services? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.)On December 3rd, 2025, the Bureau announced a significant change to that question. Here's the replacement:In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.)No more "producing goods or services" - now it's "in any of its business functions"! This means that the answers to the question before and after November 17th are not directly comparable.From October 19, 2026, they ask about Super IntelligenceWhen I went looking for the updated question language in the latest XLSX file, I couldn't find it. I found this instead:In the last two weeks, did this business use Super Intelligence or SI (formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of SI use include: SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service; SI-powered forecasting or pricing; SI-driven computer vision for quality control, etc.)The current numbers reflect the old Artificial Intelligence survey wording - the first survey results reflecting the Super Intelligence wording are due for publication on Thursday.Is this going to affect the survey?The obvious open question here is whether this wording change is going to affect the survey results.The businesses answering this survey will have last seen that question twelve weeks ago, when it was still called AI. Hopefully the new language isn't going to confuse them, especially since the survey helpfully spells out "formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI".I can't help but laugh at the absurdity of "SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service" though.

item.title: The Ten Best Captain Picard Episodes of Star Trek
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: In the wake of Patrick Stewart’s death the other day, I watched a couple episodes of Star Trek: The Next Generation — the two-part series finale All Good Things… in fact. Wanting to add more Picard-centric episodes to my watchlist, I did some research.There are several lists out there of the episodes of ST:TNG and Star Trek: Picard where Captain Jean-Luc Picard particularly shines. Some episodes appear on nearly every list; these are the consensus favorites: “Captain Jean-Luc Picard is struck unconscious by an energy beam from an alien probe. While just 25 minutes pass for the rest of the crew between Picard being struck unconscious and eventually regaining consciousness on the Enterprise bridge floor, the probe makes Picard experience 40 years of lifetime as Kamin, a humanoid scientist whose planet is threatened by the nova of its sun.” “Captain Jean-Luc Picard visits his brother’s family in France, where he begins to come to terms with his treatment by the Borg.” “In this two part episode, the Enterprise must battle the Borg who are intent on conquering Earth, with a captured and assimilated Captain Picard as their emissary.” “The crew of the Enterprise is unable to establish meaningful communication with the crew of an alien vessel, which is resolved by the struggle of the ships’ captains to defend each other from a vicious beast.” “The plot involves Captain Jean-Luc Picard jumping through time and the formation of an anomaly that defies causality, the whole situation being a test that allows Picard to demonstrate human potential to the Q Continuum by making an intuitive leap of faith to understand the cause of, and how to eliminate, the anomaly before it destroys humanity.” “In this episode, the rights of the android officer Lt. Commander Data are threatened by a scientist who wishes to dismantle him to produce replicas of him. Captain Jean-Luc Picard fights in a Starfleet court for Data’s right of self-determination, not to be declared mere property of Starfleet, while Commander William Riker is obliged to argue on behalf of the scientist.” “While the Enterprise is evacuated for hazardous maintenance, Captain Picard must, alone, contend with thieves posing as a work crew aboard the ship. The plot has been noted for its similarity to the 1988 action film Die Hard.” “Jean-Luc Picard is relieved of command of the Enterprise and reassigned to lead a covert mission, while his replacement is assigned to deal with the Cardassians openly. The second part of the episode is noted for the intense performance of Patrick Stewart and its depiction of brutal torture and interrogation scenes.” “Q allows a supposedly deceased Captain Jean-Luc Picard to re-visit a pivotal event in his youth that he since regrets. Picard changes the past, but upon returning to the present he finds that the event made him the man he became.” “An explosion aboard the Enterprise leads to a high-level investigation headed by Admiral Norah Satie, a retired officer renowned for her skill at exposing conspiracies.”The movies seemed to be out of scope for these lists, but I’ve always loved First Contact and Picard’s unhinged pursuit of the Borg — “The line must be drawn here!”

item.title: Blue Ballots
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: I’ve been backed up, aching, and swollen with a prolonged case of blue ballots for years. No one wants to feel the release of a pent-up blue surge that sprays across an election map more than I do. While things seem promising enough to expect a climax that looks like a Diet Coked-up Steve Kornacki being fired out of a T-shirt cannon, I’m not willing to make any predictions. I’ve spent too many election nights, alienated from my fellow Americans, and moaning in the fetal position. Yes, yes, I know that the polls keep looking better and better for Dems. We’ve been told for weeks that the MAGA faithful have been eyeing the exits. I’ve seen Trump’s approval slip with each bizarre rally monologue, the latest ones oddly fixated on the posteriors of both women and men (yes, he’s an Ass Man in addition to being an Ass, Man). And it doesn’t scream confidence that Trump has already announced plans to issue pardons to Elon Musk and others, or that he’s come up with a self-declared moniker: Mr. Veto. And it seems like a bad, self-defeating sign that Trump’s final midterm pitch is being held in front of the Reflecting Pool — even DNC headquarters would have been a better choice of venue. But I’m worried. I’m worried because the American voter has let us down in the past. I’m worried about what Trump will try to do before and during the election, and I’m especially worried about the Jan 6-style malfeasance and subversion that the known insurrectionist and his band of sycophantic, dictator-tot, co-conspirators will pull after the election. But if ever there were a person and a party that deserved to be covered in the shame of an oppositional tsunami, it’s these guys. Come on, America. If you don’t blow it, I finally can.+ Peter Wehner channels my concerns, and my hope, in the (Gift Article): The MAGA Reckoning Arrives. “The election, and especially the reelection, of Donald Trump caused me, for the first time in my life, to question the fundamental decency of America. I could not understand how anyone, especially my co-religionists, could look at such a squalid figure and vote for him, let alone support him enthusiastically. How could they defend his indecency time after time after time? Doesn’t partisanship have limits? Don’t honor and integrity matter? Isn’t Trump’s peculiar form of madness an obvious disqualifier? For tens of millions of Americans—more than 77 million in 2024 alone—the answer has been no. That stain is now a permanent part of the American story. But the story isn’t over. We can move beyond this grotesque chapter to something better, though the path won’t be smooth. Even if Democrats sweep the midterms, Trump will still be president, and his closing act will likely involve trying to tear the country apart. We can’t allow him to do that. We need to get to the other side of this era with our institutions, our bonds to one another, and our commitment to justice and the rule of law intact, and then begin the work of reclaiming American ideals. A wipeout of the party of Trump on Tuesday would be an awfully helpful step in that direction.”I just hope that the end of campaign season brings an end to the deluge of political spam texts. About half of mine address someone named John. But sadly, they are not Dear John letters. Dhruv Mehrotra feels our pain in : My Journey to the Center of America’s Political Spam Text Hell. “For years, I diligently opted out. I’ve replied ‘STOP’ 49 times since 2021, by my phone’s count. Sometimes ‘Stop2End,’ when that was the magic word. In November 2025, I told Jon Ossoff’s campaign some version of ‘stop.’ It did not stop. Since then, I’ve received 13 more texts boosting his campaign, from nine different numbers. When the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee texted to inform me that Bill Clinton, Barack Obama, and Joe Biden were calling me personally to action, I replied ‘eat shit.’ That didn’t work either.” (It says everything about what the internet has become that the most commonly typed word among humans is, .)My niece announced to our global family chat that she’s been supporting the Valkeries “from the start.” And she’s right. But “the start” wasn’t too long ago. The Valkeries, as it turns out, only have fair-weather fans since the weather has been fair since the team has existed. In only their second year, a band of misfits, castoffs, and also-rans just took home the WNBA championship in the league’s first Game 7. Gabby Williams’ 30-point night leads Valkyries over Dream in Game 7 for team’s first championship.+ I’ve never seen a brand (let alone a sports team brand) evolve this quickly. “Even the biggest women’s basketball events often have a way of feeling niche. Not so within the Bay Area, where the Valkyries have sold out every home game since their inception. And Game 7 was a capital-E Event in the minds of everyday commuters, Uber drivers, hotel receptionists, and flight attendants. In just two years, the Valkyries have given their fans, players, and staff something that many professional sports franchises spend decades trying to create: a genuine sense of identity, purpose, and belonging.” The Golden State Valkyries Just Changed the WNBA Forever. “Corruption is topping voter concerns in recent polls, dominating Democratic messaging, and forcing Republicans to play defense in red states. If that marks a sharp shift from recent American elections, in which such allegations have played a relatively minor role, it mirrors a growing global trend. Around the world, a backlash against corruption has roused voters and undercut populist, right-wing politicians.” (Gift Article): The Backlash to Corruption Is Going Global. (So, it seems, are protests: German Protests Turn Violent as Activists Clash With Police.)+ Getting Even With Stevens: “The about-face by Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Michigan) to endorse Republican Mike Rogers — and appear with him at a Detroit church Sunday, instead of at an event she had been scheduled to attend with El-Sayed — triggered denunciations by Democratic leaders nationwide, along with an apparent surge in fundraising for El-Sayed.” El-Sayed campaign reports $2.4 million fundraising day as Stevens endorses GOP rival.+ “A federal magistrate judge on Monday threw out charges against two former F.B.I. intelligence officials accused of lying to Congress, excoriating prosecutors for what he described as a failure of one of their most basic responsibilities: showing there was any probable cause that crimes had been committed in the first place.” (Little details like that aren’t going to stop this DOJ anytime soon, especially when it comes to enemies and elections.)+ “As durably profitable as it has been for celebrities to arbitrage their fanbase’s attention and affection, they should remember that for it to remain so, people do still have to like them. Continuing to cheerfully feed regular people into gambling’s meat grinder might not be the safest bet.” Amanda Mull in (Gift Article): Do Celebrities Endorsing Prediction Markets Not Have Enough Money Already?+ “The man who helped develop the technology for liquid crystal displays — the screens in flat-panel televisions and laptops — has died at 101.” That Giant HDTV That Fits in Your Living Room? Thank Cyril Hilsum. And he may have left us with something even more precious. A guide to longevity. “Dr. Hilsum died on Sept. 23 at an assisted-living facility in London, his family said. He was 101, having survived into his 11th decade by avoiding fresh vegetables and subsisting largely on TV dinners, chocolate and red wine.”+ “Once you see a snake in Bangkok, the snakiest capital in the world, you see snakes everywhere … On an average half-day shift, Mr. Pinyo, the top snake catcher in Thailand’s capital, wrangles more than 20 snakes, the reptiles secreted in sewers, curled in flowerpots and toilets, enmeshed in recycling, and pressed against branches ready to snack on geckoes and tree shrews. He catches cobras, pythons, kraits and pit vipers. Those are the scary snakes. Harmless species, at least to humans, include tree snakes, rat snakes, kukris and sunbeams.” This is probably not what Pinyo Pukpinyo expected when he signed up to be a firefighter. He’s the Top Snake Catcher, and Business Is Booming. There’s Just One Problem.“In ancient myth, Achilles and Patroclus were two Greek heroes of the Trojan war whose intense bond was believed by some to have turned into a sexual relationship. In modern science, they are a bull, Achille, and a donkey, Patroclo, whose tender interspecies affair has helped to shed new light on social and sexual interactions between animals.” Tender bond between male donkey and bull baffles scientists.+ David Letterman and Matt Damon as extras on The Gilded Age? Sure, why not?

item.title: Kali Malone
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today we’re listening to Kali Malone, an American organist, synthesist, and composer from Colorado. We’ve recommended her music threetimesbefore. She sang choir growing up and played piano and guitar; she also spent time “busking, sleeping on beaches, crashing at weed farms, bartering,” to quote ’s excellent interview with Malone. After a chance encounter with the composer Ellen Arkbro in New York, she relocated to Stockholm and enrolled in the Royal College of Music. She studied historic tuning, with a focus on church organs. Her new record, , came out on Friday. It was recorded at St. Thomas Church in Leipzig on the “Bach organ,” a replica of the 1696 organ J.S. Bach’s uncle designed and which influenced the young composer. Like her preceding records, draws out the organ’s notes, demonstrating the “unequal temperament” or variable frequency graduations across this particular instrument. The performance, with Sunn O)))’s Stephen O’Malley (guitar) and Lucy Railton (cello), was captured on 20 microphones, placed close up to the organ and across the room, creating an immersive listening experience. All that said, Laura Snapes wrote in the Guardian, “In drone world, Burning Song is Kali Malone’s pop record.” By contrast, , Malone’s record from 2023 with the same accompanists, is over five hours.We wish you a great start to your week.

item.title: The Cars – “You Might Think” vs. Huey Lewis & the News – “The Power of Love”
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: The 1980s produced an incredible number of pop-rock songs that managed to be commercially successful, musically distinctive, and permanently attached to the decade’s cultural identity. Two outstanding examples are The Cars’ “You Might Think” and Huey Lewis & the News’ “The Power of Love.” Both songs arrived during the golden age of MTV, both became defining hits for their respective artists, and both demonstrated how a great hook could turn a straightforward rock song into a pop-culture institution.Released in 1984, “You Might Think” showcased The Cars’ ability to combine new wave eccentricity with polished, radio-friendly songwriting. A year later, “The Power of Love” became one of the signature songs of the era, pairing Huey Lewis’s energetic vocals with a driving rock arrangement that practically demanded to be played at maximum volume.One song is quirky, sophisticated, and unmistakably new wave. The other is muscular, exuberant, and built around the kind of chorus that can fill an arena. Which deserves the crown? Let’s put them through ten rounds of musical combat.Song Spotlight: The Cars – “You Might Think”Appearing on the 1984 album , “You Might Think” captures The Cars at their commercial and creative peak. Ric Ocasek’s songwriting combines nervous romantic obsession with a playful melody, while the band’s trademark blend of synthesizers, electric guitars, and precise rhythms gives the track its distinctive character.The production is bright and meticulously arranged, but the song never feels sterile. The guitars provide a satisfying crunch, the keyboards add a futuristic sheen, and the rhythm section keeps everything moving. Ocasek’s understated vocals are central to the appeal. Rather than delivering an oversized rock performance, he sounds like someone casually explaining a ridiculous situation, which makes the song’s eccentricity even more effective.The accompanying music video became a landmark of the MTV era, using imaginative visual effects and surreal transformations to match the song’s offbeat personality. “You Might Think” was more than another successful single; it was an example of how The Cars could make unconventional ideas sound completely accessible.Song Spotlight: Huey Lewis & the News – “The Power of Love”Released in 1985, “The Power of Love” became one of Huey Lewis & the News’ biggest hits and an essential part of the soundtrack. The song’s success was no accident. Its opening guitar riff establishes an immediate sense of momentum, the rhythm section drives the arrangement forward, and Huey Lewis delivers the vocals with the confidence of a frontman who understands exactly how to command a crowd.The band’s blend of rock, pop, and R&B gives the song a muscular, celebratory quality. Everything feels designed to build toward that enormous chorus, which remains one of the most instantly recognizable hooks of the decade.Its connection to Marty McFly’s adventures helped give the song a cultural life beyond the charts. Yet “The Power of Love” is more than a movie tie-in. It is a superbly constructed rock single that showcases the band’s ability to make polished, accessible music without sacrificing energy.Round 1: The Opening Hook“You Might Think” immediately establishes its identity through bright keyboards, crisp guitars, and a melody that feels slightly off-kilter in the best possible way. The Cars waste no time getting to the song’s infectious central idea, and the arrangement keeps the listener engaged through its carefully placed instrumental details.“The Power of Love” counters with a chunky guitar riff that announces itself with considerably more muscle. Its groove is direct, confident, and immediately recognizable. Huey Lewis and the News know how to make a song sound enormous without overcomplicating the arrangement.Both openings are excellent, but The Cars offer a more distinctive combination of sounds and melodic personality.Round Winner: The Cars – “You Might Think.”Round 2: Vocal PerformanceRic Ocasek’s vocal delivery is an essential part of The Cars’ identity. His slightly detached, conversational style gives “You Might Think” an unusual charm. He never sounds like he is trying too hard, and that restraint makes the song’s obsessive romantic perspective amusing rather than melodramatic.Huey Lewis takes the opposite approach. His voice is fuller, bluesier, and more forceful, bringing a natural enthusiasm to “The Power of Love.” He sounds like a frontman who could deliver the song to a packed stadium and have every person singing along by the second chorus.Ocasek is perfectly suited to his song, but Lewis demonstrates greater vocal power and range of expression.Round Winner: Huey Lewis & the News – “The Power of Love.”The chorus of “You Might Think” is a master class in economical pop songwriting. Its central hook is simple enough to remember after one listen, but the melody has enough personality to avoid sounding generic. The Cars make the refrain feel playful, slightly obsessive, and effortlessly catchy.“The Power of Love” delivers a more explosive chorus. The arrangement opens up, the vocal becomes more commanding, and the song takes on the feeling of a full-scale celebration. It is the sort of refrain that works equally well on the radio, in a movie, or in front of thousands of concertgoers.The Cars have the more eccentric hook, but Huey Lewis and the News deliver the bigger payoff.Round Winner: Huey Lewis & the News – “The Power of Love.”Round 4: Instrumentation and MusicianshipThe Cars excel at making every instrument serve the song. The guitars and synthesizers complement one another rather than competing for attention, while the rhythm section provides a precise foundation. The production allows individual details to emerge without disrupting the track’s forward momentum.“The Power of Love” relies on a more traditional rock arrangement, but that approach is executed exceptionally well. The guitar work gives the song its backbone, the bass and drums establish an irresistible groove, and the band sounds completely comfortable in its chosen style.This is a close contest between precision and propulsion. The Cars’ arrangement is more distinctive, and its interplay between keyboards and guitars gives the song a slight advantage in musical character.Round Winner: The Cars – “You Might Think.”Produced by Robert John “Mutt” Lange, “You Might Think” benefits from the sleek, meticulously controlled sound that defined . Every instrument occupies its own space, the vocals remain clear, and the synthesizers add atmosphere without overwhelming the guitars. The result is a polished recording that still retains The Cars’ personality.“The Power of Love” sounds equally comfortable in its own sonic environment. Its production emphasizes punch, clarity, and momentum. The guitar riff cuts through the mix, the drums provide a strong foundation, and the chorus feels appropriately oversized without becoming cluttered.Both recordings are superb examples of mid-1980s studio craft. However, “You Might Think” integrates its electronic and rock elements with slightly greater originality.Round Winner: The Cars – “You Might Think.”The Cars had already established a recognizable sound by the time “You Might Think” arrived, but the song still feels unusual. Its combination of nervous romantic subject matter, deadpan vocals, bright keyboards, and angular pop-rock arrangements gives it an identity that few other bands could convincingly reproduce.“The Power of Love” is an outstanding example of mainstream rock songwriting, but its ingredients are more familiar. A commanding guitar riff, a strong vocal, a driving rhythm, and an enormous chorus are classic components of the genre. Huey Lewis and the News execute them brilliantly, yet the song is less adventurous in its construction.Originality is where The Cars establish a meaningful advantage. Their song sounds like a world of its own rather than simply a particularly good example of a familiar formula.Round Winner: The Cars – “You Might Think.”Round 7: Music Video and Visual Impact“You Might Think” became one of the defining videos of early MTV, embracing computer-generated imagery and surreal visual effects at a time when the technology was still relatively novel. The bizarre transformations and playful imagery perfectly complemented the song’s personality. The video also won Video of the Year at the inaugural MTV Video Music Awards in 1984.“The Power of Love” benefits from its association with . The movie connection gives the song a narrative and cultural context that has helped it remain recognizable across generations. It is an effective promotional video and a memorable piece of 1980s entertainment.Nevertheless, The Cars delivered the more groundbreaking visual experience. Their video was not simply a way to sell a single; it helped expand the creative possibilities of the medium.Round Winner: The Cars – “You Might Think.”“You Might Think” was a major hit and an important part of The Cars’ commercial peak. Its music video helped establish the band as an MTV-era powerhouse, and the song remains closely associated with the sound and style of mid-1980s pop-rock.“The Power of Love” has an especially powerful cultural advantage: . The song became inseparable from one of the decade’s most beloved films, giving it exposure to audiences who might never have discovered Huey Lewis & the News through radio alone. Its chart success and enduring movie association have kept it firmly embedded in popular culture.The Cars made the more innovative artistic statement, but the combination of a major hit and a legendary film gives Huey Lewis the edge here.Round Winner: Huey Lewis & the News – “The Power of Love.”Round 9: Longevity and Replay Value“You Might Think” remains a highly enjoyable listen because its appeal extends beyond nostalgia. The arrangement contains enough little details to reward repeated listening, and the song’s unusual personality prevents it from becoming just another dated artifact of the MTV era.“The Power of Love” has tremendous replay value as well. Its direct songwriting, infectious groove, and association with make it an easy choice for classic-rock playlists, movie-themed events, and nostalgic listening sessions. The chorus is as effective today as it was in 1985.Both songs have aged remarkably well. The Cars win narrowly because their more distinctive arrangement gives listeners additional musical details to appreciate with repeated plays.Round Winner: The Cars – “You Might Think.”Round 10: The Ultimate Feel-Good Factor“You Might Think” is fun in a slightly strange, intellectually playful way. Its melody is infectious, its lyrics have a humorous edge, and its arrangement creates an atmosphere of bright, quirky optimism. It is the kind of song that makes you appreciate the wonderfully odd things that mainstream pop music could accomplish in the 1980s.“The Power of Love” is pure, uncomplicated exhilaration. The groove makes you want to move, the chorus invites everyone to sing along, and the performance radiates confidence. It is tailor-made for road trips, parties, and those moments when a familiar song instantly improves the atmosphere.The Cars make you smile, but Huey Lewis and the News make you want to turn up the volume and sing along at the top of your lungs.Round Winner: Huey Lewis & the News – “The Power of Love.”The final score is The Cars 6, Huey Lewis & the News 4.“You Might Think” takes the overall victory by offering the more distinctive musical identity. Its inventive arrangement, carefully controlled production, memorable melody, and groundbreaking video make it a particularly strong representation of what made 1980s pop-rock so exciting. The Cars understood how to combine commercial songwriting with an eccentric streak that kept their music from sounding ordinary.“The Power of Love” puts up an impressive fight. Huey Lewis delivers the stronger vocal performance, the bigger chorus, and the more immediately celebratory listening experience. Its connection to also gives it an enduring cultural advantage that few singles can match.Ultimately, this battle comes down to innovation versus pure rock-and-roll exhilaration. Huey Lewis and the News made the kind of song that could unite an entire room, while The Cars created a track with a little more personality and a sound that remains uniquely their own.The Winner: The Cars – “You Might Think.”Sometimes the best song isn’t the loudest or the biggest hit. Sometimes it’s the one that manages to be catchy, strange, sophisticated, and completely irresistible all at once.

item.title: Michigan/Stevens Folly Continues
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: From what I can tell, the details on Haley Stevens’s last 36 hours, which I reported earlier this afternoon, have now been confirmed, re-reported by the Post and other publications. Appreciate the congrats. I think the best bet is that we, political obsessives, are overestimating how much this whole drama will affect the outcome in either direction. But if it has any effect, I think there’s a decent chance it will actually redound to Abdul El-Sayed’s benefit. One of the things that’s been hard to miss over the course of the day is the sheer intensity of the denunciations of Stevens from the highest ranks of the Democratic Party, including many of her one-time supporters. That has many sources — but one of the biggest is that, as I reported earlier, she told many of these people, , last night that she was absolutely still going to vote for El-Sayed. So they feel personally very burned.

item.title: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded:
I've been getting the occasional confusing Python dependency error since switching over to Python 3.15 and the rule I'm having to remember is:If in doubt, delete the uv.lock fileMost of my projects are libraries which don't include a file, since it's rude for a library dependency to lock versions for anything else that uses it.Running etc tends to leave files lying around, which are listed in and so do not get committed to my repositories.But... sometimes that pins a version of a dependency that doesn't yet have a Python 3.15 wheel. An example from earlier today:error: Failed to build `watchfiles==1.1.1` cause: Call to `maturin.build_wheel` failed
error: the configured Python interpreter version (3.15) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version (3.14) Deleting that file and running again usually fixes the problem.

item.title: “That lawyer is me”: Why Trump’s threats won’t stop me
item.author: 1axcj8xc1zjewmopzejbfpl8mn3axv6p0mz2jn@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: He will try to pressure us to back away from protecting voting rights. He will try to force us to stay silent.Trump’s many attacks on me are well known.In 2018, he called me the Democratic Party’s “best Election stealing lawyer.” Two years later, I helped lead the effort to defeat his attempts to overturn the 2020 election in more than 60 court cases, election contests and recounts.In 2024, he posted an article titled “Marc Elias Is Scared ... And He Should Be” and twice posted that, if elected, he intended to investigate and prosecute “Lawyers” he saw as helping political opponents.He has followed through. In a March 2025 speech at the Justice Department, he called me and another lawyer “radicals” trying to turn America into a “corrupt, communist, third-world country.”About a week later, he issued a presidential memorandum targeting me and my law firm by name. By then, he had already tried to sanction my prior law firm, citing work I did there in 2016.Earlier this year, as my firm was defeating the department in dozens of cases around the country, he called me “a terrible lawyer with a horrible track record.”I could go on. I could list the times his allies have attacked me with lies, the civil lawsuit he filed against me that was dismissed, and his weaponization of government, including the criminal investigation by special counsel John Durham launched during his first term.But the point is simple. As he posted in 2024, he wants me to be scared. He wants all of us to be afraid to stand up to him.He wants us to stop speaking out. He wants us to believe that he is so powerful that there is simply no point in fighting back.To be honest, in too many places, his strategy of fear and intimidation has worked.Large law firms have sat idly by as Trump and his cronies violate the Constitution and make a mockery of the rule of law. Too afraid to offend Trump, they sit in their fancy offices while small law firms like mine litigate scores of cases.Large media outlets are in full both-sides mode, with occasional obsessions reminiscent of the “but her emails” craze of 2016. They, too, are hoping to keep their access to the White House and avoid unduly offending its current occupant.Business leaders are not just silent but complicit. They shower Trump with false praise, lavish gifts and business opportunities for his family.With the Justice Department losing in court nearly every day, I expect further escalations from Trump and his allies.Trump wants his Justice Department to be more brazen not only in its words but in its actions. Indeed, he complained to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi — in a now-famous September 2025 Truth Social post — that people saw her department as “all talk, no action” and that “nothing is being done.”Election Day is Tuesday, but the fight against Trump’s attacks on democracy will continue. Trump can try to intimidate me. He can try to scare. But I have never backed down before — and I will not start now.

item.title: The Buccaneers Played Prehistoric Football And Won
item.author: Tom Ley
item.content:encoded: It's wise to never expect too much from a clash between two NFC South teams. They tend to be a form of stultifying anti-entertainment, and so Sunday's game between the Atlanta Falcons and Tampa Bay Buccaneers would normally be an easy skip. The NFC South has felt a little different this year, though, and not because any of its teams are playing particularly good football. What they have been doing is playing weird, entertaining football, and today the Bucs and Falcons played what might end up being the weirdest and most entertaining game of the season.A huge rainstorm rolled into Tampa, Fla., this morning, absolutely soaking the Bucs' field and creating the kind of conditions that would make any offensive coordinator squeamish about calling a passing play. Now imagine how much more stressful that scenario becomes when the quarterbacks at their disposal are Baker Mayfield and Michael Penix Jr. Facing these conditions, the Buccaneers came up with a novel strategy: What if we just didn't throw a pass?Well, OK, they threw three passes, but none of them were completed. Mayfield's final stat line: 0-for-3 for zero yards, zero touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Any football game that produces a quarterback box score like that is already a thing to behold, but this one was made truly special by the fact that the Bucs won the game, 16-0. They did so by running the ball 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell each got to live out every running back's fantasy: Irving finished with 170 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries, and Gainwell chipped in with 140 yards on 25 carries. The game's representative highlight was probably Mayfield fumbling a snap and scrambling for a few seconds before throwing a desperate backward pass to Irving, who churned through the rain and mud before fumbling the ball right at the goal line.

item.title: gobench: a tool for comparing Go benchmark runs across branches
item.author: Alex Chan
item.content:encoded: I’ve recently joined a new team that’s focused on performance, stability, and scalability – a change from my previous projects, where traffic was low enough that performance was rarely a concern.This codebase has already gone through multiple rounds of optimisation, so there’s no low-hanging fruit left. Any proposed change is inherently complex, and it’s rarely obvious whether a tweak will actually speed things up or slow them down. To measure the impact of our work, we’re leaning on the benchmarking tools in Go’s standard library.On one of my recent pull requests, I wrote a benchmark, and I pasted the output from two before/after runs. Paul improved this with a short shell script that ran multiple samples, and compared the results with the benchstat command.N..6C613000cfc12d4cecho$N:$Cgitcheckout-q$C./tool/gotest-run^X-benchBenchmarkPostureAnalyzer./control/posture/analysis/tee-abench-$C.txtbenchstatbench-fc12d4c.txtbench-613000c.txtbenchstat does statistical analysis on the output from multiple runs, which is more reliable and easier to read than the raw output. In particular, it puts all the data in a single table, and shows the percentage change against the baseline.I like this script, but it’s a little fiddly. I have to identify the two commits to compare, it leaves text files in my working directory, and it leaves my repo in a detached head state when it’s done. I wanted something more ergonomic.I’ve written a new tool gobench to give me a smoother experience. I check out my feature branch, run gobench with the arguments I’d pass to , and it prints the final analysis from benchstat.Under the hood, it creates a Git work tree for the base branch (leaving my working directory as-is), captures the benchmark output in memory (so there are no extra text files), and does an alternating sample of benchmarks.The alternating samples is a feature I really like from Paul’s original script. I run benchmarks on my laptop rather than a dedicated workstation, and the benchmarks could be sensitive to thermal throttling, background processes, or other things happening on my computer. Alternating between the two branches reduces the effect of this noise.Let’s look at an example. Suppose my main branch has a recursive implementation of Fibonacci numbers, while my feature branch has an iterative approach. Unsurprisingly, the iterative approach is faster, and gobench makes it easy to quantify the improvement.gorun./cmd/gobench./example/fib/-benchBenchmarkFib My first version of gobench was an expansion of Paul’s script, but as I started adding features, it became clear that Bash was the wrong tool. I rewrote it as a Go tool that shells out to , , and .If you’d like to try gobench yourself, the code is available in my gotools repository, or you can install it with:goinstallalexwlchan.net/gotools/cmd/gobench@latestgobench has already saved me from shipping code that looked fast on paper but regressed in practice. As I keep working on performance-critical Go code, having low-friction benchmarks will make it easier to test my ideas early and often.

item.title: Pathetic Crybaby Haley Stevens Endorses Mike Rogers
item.author: Tom Ley
item.content:encoded: If one thing's been made clear through the last decade or so of national politics, it's that there are John Fettermans hiding in plain sight throughout the Democratic Party. The latest member to don the Mantle Of The Oaf is Haley Stevens, who lost her primary race for a Senate seat to Abdul El-Sayed this summer. Now, a few days before the general election, she has endorsed El-Sayed's Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.Stevens appeared Sunday morning with Rogers at a church service in Detroit. While entering the venue, she stopped to tell reporters that she's in favor of investing in black-owned businesses, adding, "that’s the policy that Mike’s going to take on." She then sat in the same row as Rogers during the service. https://twitter.com/samueljrob/status/2116928933740298485

item.title: Gabby Williams And The Valks Are Golden
item.author: Maitreyi Anantharaman
item.content:encoded: What now? Any ideas? The Golden State Valkyries trailed the Atlanta Dream by six at halftime, and every point in this series felt like a hundred. The Valks will tell you theirs is an “egoless” team, one on which no one is above a scramble for a loose ball or a box-out. Zero All-WNBA players. Zero MVPs. The concept of “MV” wouldn’t even sit right with them. That spirit carried them far in the regular season, kept them fresh for the postseason, and made them nimble enough to handle a mid-series shake-up to the starting lineup. So committed were they to this formula that even six games in, Finals MVP really was anyone’s for the taking. Only no one was taking it. If you have 10 stars on your team, you have none. Basketball is a team sport, but even its team-iest sequences end in something individual. For the ball to get through the net, one player has to entertain a selfish thought: , or or I can get this shot up faster than you can get here. Gabby Williams, Golden State’s only All-Star selection this year, was brought here in the offseason to be that player. But for six games, scoring—even finding decent shots to take—had been a pain for her, and 20 minutes into the seventh, it didn’t seem like the struggle was letting up. She finished with two points at the half, having scored zero in the first quarter and the two on only one field goal attempt in the second. At some point in the third, though, you could see it all dawn on her. She is stronger than the Dream’s point guard, Jordin Canada, whom she hunted in switches. She is a former track champion who is faster than everyone else on the floor. Just like that, she was the most confident player out there, her heat-check threes bringing life back into Ballhalla in a 28-point second half for the ages.When it all clicked, Williams solved two problems: After a 68-63 Game 7 win in a sometimes stomach-turning series, the Golden State Valkyries are WNBA champions in the franchise’s second year. The eventual Finals MVP finished with 30 points, three rebounds, two assists, two steals and four blocks.

item.title: Haley Stevens’ High(est) Profile Meltdown
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Let me share a few quick thoughts about former Democratic Senate primary candidate Haley Stevens. As you’ve likely seen, Stevens showed up this morning at a Black church in Detroit with Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers. Let me say first that my best guess is that Abdul El-Sayed is going to win this race and that all this final-days drama with Stevens won’t end up to have mattered. I will also say that I can’t remember a spectacle quite like this, or any defeated Democratic primary candidate crashing out like this, in 30-plus years of observing Democratic politics very, very closely.On Friday I said that while to that point I’d questioned Stevens’ judgment, wisdom and decision-making, I was now questioning her sanity. That was only slightly tongue-in-cheek. And even less so now. There’s a level of erratic, boffo behavior here that is even more than appears on the surface. From a mix of watching the morning shows and my own reporting, I can tell you that as recently as last night Stevens told multiple Democratic power players that she was still going to vote for Abdul El-Sayed. As I’m writing this, in addition to the church appearance, I’ve just seen that she is now officially endorsing Mike Rogers. She seems to be blaming that to some degree on that fact that she was disinvited from today’s Democratic unity rally. But whatever you think of Stevens and El-Sayed, her statement in advance of that rally made disinviting her unavoidable. She quite literally forced it.

item.title: Three More Women Say Josh Jacobs Physically Abused Them
item.author: Tom Ley
item.content:encoded: On Friday, the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department released a batch of records related to Packers running back Josh Jacobs's domestic violence arrest in May. The records reveal that while police were investigating the May incident, they were contacted by three other women who said Jacobs abused them in the past. One document describes a phone conversation a police investigator had with a woman, who said she felt compelled to contact police after learning about the details of Jacobs's May arrest. According to the report, this woman told the investigator that she was abused by Jacobs in 2023 after meeting him in his house. She told police that she went to Jacobs's house after meeting him on Instagram. The woman claims that when she arrived at the house, Jacobs questioned whether she had come to have sex with him. When she said that wasn't the reason she came to the house, she says he became angry and slapped her across the face. The woman also told police that Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, pinned her to the bed, threw her off the bed, spit on her, grabbed her by the throat, and said, "I should kill you right now."The woman told the investigator that she did not contact the police at the time because she remained friends with Jacobs after the incident and was worried people wouldn't believe her.

item.title: It’s Sunday. Let’s celebrate some heroes.
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Yes, I know. Everything right now. But that doesn’t mean we can’t occasionally pause to celebrate the heroes within our midst.Today, let’s do just that.Sir Patrick Stewart passed away this week at the age of 86. During his life, he’d been a Shakespearean actor, a starship captain, and a role model, beloved by millions. But here’s another fun fact about Sir Pat: he fuckingDonny Convict. Check out this except from an interview Stewart did with the AV Club back in 2017.“You might say to me, ‘well, you’re not an American. What has it got to do with you?’ The fact is, when America sneezes, the world catches a cold. And America, I think, is on the edge of a very bad flu infection. And it’s because of the man who is in the White House. I do find, as time goes by, I find myself becoming increasingly anxious.”“I’m not a citizen,” he said. “However, there is, maybe it’s the only good thing, as the result of this election: I am now applying for citizenship. Because I want to be an American too.”He added, “All of my friends in Washington said, ‘There is one thing you can do. Fight, fight, oppose, oppose.’”Congratulations, Donny — you’re now an inspiration. Stand proud. No one every became a citizen just so they could vote against Joe Biden. You built that! (Full disclosure: in the interest of Responsible Journalism and Everything™, I asked Google’s janky, six-fingered plagiarism robot if Patrick Stewart ever did become a US citizen. Sadly, the answer was ‘no,’ for a number of reasons. I don’t care. Sir Patrick is still a hero.)Here’s another hero — actor Wil Wheaton, who played Ensign Crusher on Star Trek: The Next Generation.Stephen Miller, on behalf of Star Trek, and everyone who knew and loved him, keep my Captain’s name out of your fucking Nazi mouth. He despised you, and everything you stand for.Hang on, we should probably to do a quick fact check. Does Nosferatu McGoebbels. in fact have a ‘fucking Nazi mouth’?Yes — yes he does. And I would add to the mix.Look, I’m with Wil. Nosferatu needs to shut the fuck up. Whatever lessons he imagines he learned from watching Star Trek as a kid, he clearly got it wrong. There are no episodes where the fascist fuckwads are the guys. How does one watch Star Trek and come away with the conclusion that the racist oppressors are the icons? Not all heroes wear capes. Sometimes they stand in the audience and yell shit.I believe it was Jesus who so wisely counseled us in his Sermon on the Mount, ‘blessed are the hecklers, because they make the shit-gizzards we hate look like stupid dicks.’It’s not just Dear Leader bearing the brunt of it. Republicans coast to coast are getting an earful from their fed-up constituents. Ken Paxton: “Talk your friends. Talk to your family. Tell them the difference between me and James Talarico.”Audience member: “Paxton, you take bribes!”My god, is Ken Paxton the least-magnetic candidate, like, ever? He just stands there, farting tepid mouth-sounds out of his face-hole. He makes Couchfuck McGee seem like the most dynamic public speaker in the multiverse.Who is supposed to walk away from this sleepwalked drivel, inspired to vote?Can’t Paxton find himself a job where he can steal all the money he wants without having to bore people to death at the same time? Is that really too much to ask?I have no idea who this couple is, or where they were. I learned about it from opening my social feeds last night, and there was this clip, all over the place. All I know is that we need to gif that shit, pronto.Holy shit, that’s some nightmare fuel right here. Fucking terrifying.Folks, I’ve got one more hero for you. My very good friend Eliza Gilkyson has a new album coming out early next year.This week, she posted a song from the album, to both Facebook and YouTube. Please give it a listen. I promise you, ‘In America’ is the first single from my upcoming album, LIFELINE, to be released in Feb., and due to its political nature, Facebook is not allowing me to boost the song during election week. So they have totally held me back, and that’s where you come in. We are allowed to post it, just not boost it. So if you can post the song on any of your socials and let your friends know they can do the same, then we can defy the muzzle order and let this song find its way to other like-minded souls during this worrisome week ahead of us.Wouldn’t it be nice if we lived in a world where our tech-bro overlords didn’t tip the scales in favor of the fascists? What kind of un-American bullshit is ‘you can’t boost a political song before an election’? That’s unthinkable. What the fuck has happened to our country?What episode of Star Trek was Zuck watching when he came away with the notion that being a greedy, oligarchic piece of shit was the true way forward? Because I don’t remember that one.Oh, look. We’re down at the bottom of the post. You know what that means. It’s Daily Claudia time.Today, let’s revisit cocktail hour on the patio of the Coast Guard House in Narragansett, Rhode Island, on September 21, 2023.Have a great Sunday, everyone. here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.
